Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry, fold into batter with rubber spatula just to combine.
Heat waffle iron. Ladle in 3/4 cups batter.
Cook each waffle 4 minutes or until indicator light on machine goes on.

recipes.name: Beet and Apple Juice
instructions: Cut produce to fit juicer feed tube.
Alternate juicing beets and apples, finishing with beets. Refrigerate juice 5-10 minutes for foam to settle.
Scrape off any excess foam and serve immediately.

recipes.name: BEET KVASS
instructions: Place beets in bottom of jar, add whey/juice (if using), and salt as needed.
Cover beets with water, place cheesecloth over mouth of jar and secure with string.
Set in cool dark spot for 2 days to ferment if using whey/juice or 3 days without.
Strain beets from liquid, and discard beets. Return liquid to jar and refrigerate.

recipes.name: BLUEBERRY CORN MUFFINS
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 400°F. Grease muffin pan with butter.
In medium bowl, combine dry ingredients.
In separate small bowl, combine wet ingredients: butter, milk, maple syrup, and eggs.
Mix wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Add blueberries. Mix carefully to incorporate.
Using standard ice cream scoop, fill muffin tins 3/4 full.
Bake 15-18 minutes. Best served warm.

recipes.name: Blueberry Muffins
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350°F. Line muffin pans with paper liners and set aside.
In medium bowl, sift flours, baking powder, baking soda, and spices together and whisk to combine.
In separate bowl, whisk together oat milk, kuzu, melted coconut oil, maple syrup, vinegar, and salt. Pour wet mixture into dry ingredients bowl. Whisk to combine. Gently stir in blueberries.

With 1-ounce scoop, pour batter into muffin papers to fill almost to top (about 3/4 full). Transfer muffin tins to half sheet pans. Bake 5-6 minutes, rotate pans, and continue to bake (about 6-8 minutes more) until top of muffins bounces back when touched and toothpick comes out clean.
Remove muffins from pans immediately and cool completely before serving.

recipes.name: Blueberry Syrup
instructions: Combine all ingredients in 2 1/2 quart pot. Bring syrup to boil, reduce heat, and simmer mixture uncovered for 15 minutes.
Strain syrup through chinois, pressing any remaining juice from blueberries. Discard blueberries, and transfer syrup to syrup containers.

recipes.name: BUCKWHEAT PANCAKES
recipes.description: Vegan
instructions: In medium bowl, combine flours, baking powder, salt, baking soda, and maple crystals. Set aside.
In separate bowl, combine apple cider vinegar, and almond milk. Let sit for 5-10 minutes. Add banana.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Beat batter only until blended.
Using 1-ounce ladle, pour batter onto griddle. Cook cakes until bubbles in batter break on t surface; flip and cook until browned.

recipes.name: BUTTERMILK-STYLE WAFFLES
recipes.description: (Vegan)

ingredients.name: aquafaba strained from 2 cans of chickpeas

instructions: Heat waffle iron. In bowl, whisk together almond milk and vinegar. Set aside and let stand 15 minutes.
In medium bowl, whisk together to combine flour, baking soda and cream of tartar.
In separate bowl, whisk yolk with milk mixture and oil.
Beat egg white to stiff peak.

Add milk mixture to dry ingredients in thin, steady stream, while gently mixing with rubber spatula; be careful not to add liquid faster than it can be incorporated. Toward end of mixing, use folding motion to incorporate aqua faba.
Spread appropriate amount of batter onto waffle iron. Following manufacturer's instructions, cook waffle until golden brown, at least 5 minutes.

recipes.name: CARROT-CELERY-GINGER JUICE
instructions: Cut produce to fit juicer feed tube. Juice produce alternating ingredients (parsley, celery, lemon, ginger, carrots, parsley, etc.).
Skim foam and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Cashew Milk
instructions: Puree cashews and water in Vitamix until cashews are completely pulverized. Strain milk through chinois.

recipes.name: CASHEW MILK (FOR SWEET VEGAN CRÊPES)
instructions: Puree mixture in VitaMix or blender. Strain through chinois or strainer lined with wet cheesecloth.

recipes.name: Challah
instructions: Combine water and honey. Sprinkle yeast on top of mixture. Set aside until foamy.
Add eggs, butter, and salt. Add flour, one cup at a time, stirring until dough comes together.
Turn dough out onto lightly floured surface and knead to form smooth, pliable dough (about 10 minutes), adding flour as necessary.
Transfer dough to large, clean, lightly oiled bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let rise in warm area until doubled in size (about 1 hour).
Turn and fold dough. Cover and rise again (about 1/2 hour).
Divide dough into two large balls. Divide each ball evenly into equal portions for braiding. Roll divided dough into long strips of equal length.

To braid, pinch strips together at top. Braid both breads, transferring each to separate parchment-lined sheet tray. Cover breads with damp towels, and rise one more time (15-20 minutes), until doubled in size.
While bread is rising, pre-heat oven to 350°F.
Glaze bread with egg wash and bake until golden brown and fully cooked (inner temp about 190°F).
Transfer breads to cooling racks and fully cool before slicing.

recipes.name: "CHEESE" MEDALLIONS (FOR SPINACH-SHIITAKE SALAD)
instructions: Combine cashews, lemon juice, miso, salt, coconut oil, and boiling water in food processor. Process for 1 minute, or until smooth, scraping down sides occasionally. Add pectin powder and pulse until combined. Stream in calcium water as engine is running.
Transfer mixture to bowl and refrigerate for 10 to 20 minutes, or until slightly firm. Scoop into medallions using retractable ice cream scoop. Roll sides in crushed pistachios.

recipes.name: CHICKPEA CRÊPE
instructions: In large bowl, sift flours, salt, and pepper.
Add water, herbs and oil to flour mixture and blend with whisk until smooth. (May also be processed in blender.)
Let batter rest at room temperature at least 30 minutes. If necessary, thin batter with more water to maintain consistency of light cream.

Prepare crêpe pan by oiling lightly. Pour approximately 1/4 cup of batter into pan, tipping pan so batter thins covers pan. Cook 30 seconds, until crêpe is golden brown on bottom. Flip, cook another 30 seconds.

recipes.name: CHICKPEA CRÊPES WITH CURRIED CHICKPEAS, VEGETABLES & MANGO SAUCE
instructions: Chickpea Crêpe (recipe below):
In large bowl, sift flours, salt, and pepper.
Add water, herbs and oil to flour mixture and blend with whisk until smooth. (May also be processed in blender.)
Let batter rest at room temperature at least 30 minutes. If necessary, thin batter with more water to maintain consistency of light cream.

Prepare crêpe pan by oiling lightly. Pour approximately 1/4 cup of batter into pan, tipping pan so batter thins covers pan. Cook 30 seconds, until crêpe is golden brown on bottom. Flip, cook another 30 seconds.
Curried Chickpea Filling (recipe follows):
In pressure cooker, combine chickpeas, water, cumin, salt, and bay leaves.
Bring pot to pressure, lower heat, and cook 30 minutes. Drain beans, set aside, and reserve bean liquid if using in place of stock.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add onions. Lower heat and cook until onions begin to soften and become translucent. Add curry. Cook 2-3 minutes more.
Add carrots and potatoes, stirring often to prevent sticking. Cook 5-6 minutes. Add garlic and salt. Cook 2-3 minutes more. Add stock or bean liquid reserved from chickpeas.

Add coconut milk and chickpeas. Simmer 3-4 minutes more. Add spinach. Cook until spinach becomes tender (about 1-2 minutes). Adjust seasonings. If mixture looks too thick, add bit more stock or bean liquid.
Mango Sauce, for garnish (recipe follows):
In blender, combine mango, tomatoes, tomato juices, shallot, canola oil, lime juice, and salt. Blend until creamy.
Adjust seasonings. Garnish sauce with jalapeño and cilantro.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE PUDDING
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, over medium heat, simmer together milk, cocoa, agar, and sea salt for about 20-25 minutes, whisking to fully dissolve agar.
In small bowl, dissolve kuzu in water. Pour into saucepan with cocoa mixture, stirring until liquid returns to boil. Continue to cook one minute more until mixture is thicker.
Add maple syrup and vanilla to taste. Cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Remove pot from heat and mix some of cocoa mixture with cashew butter until cashew butter is thinner, smooth, and creamy. Whisk tempered cashew butter into cocoa mixture.
Pour cocoa mixture into shallow pan and cool until firm. In food processor, blend mixture until smooth and creamy. Spoon pudding into ramekins and chill until set (about 30 minutes).

recipes.name: Corn Muffins
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350°F. Line mini muffin pans with muffin papers and set aside.
In 8-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add onions and garlic. Cook, on medium-low heat, to caramelize (about 10-15 minutes). Remove from heat and stir in red pepper, jalapeno pepper, and cilantro. Set aside.
In medium bowl, sift cornmeal, flour, maple crystals, baking powder, and baking soda. Whisk to combine.
In separate medium bowl, whisk together oat milk, kuzu, salt, vinegar, and olive oil.
Pour wet mixture into flour mixture and gently stir with spatula just to combine then add onion/pepper mixture. Mix just enough to incorporate ingredients.

With 1-ounce scoop, pour batter into liner-filled muffin tins to almost the top (about 3/4 full). Transfer muffin tins to half sheet pans. Bake 5-6 minutes, rotate pans, and continue to bake (about 6-8 minutes more) until top of muffin bounces back when touched and toothpick comes out clean.
Remove muffins from pans immediately and cool completely before serving.

recipes.name: CORNMEAL PANCAKES (JOHNNY CAKES)
instructions: In large bowl, whisk cornmeal, salt and maple crystals. Slowly add boiling water. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
In separate bowl, beat together egg, milk and melted butter. Add to cornmeal mixture.
In separate bowl, whisk together flour and baking powder and stir into batter with few swift strokes. Add lemon zest and blueberries, if using.
Using 1-ounce ladle, pour batter onto griddle. Cook cakes until bubbles in batter break on surface; flip and cook until browned.

recipes.name: CREAMY FRESH HORSERADISH DRESSING
instructions: In blender, combine horseradish, tofu, oil, miso, soymilk, garlic, lemon, vinegar, and mustard. Process until creamy and smooth. Add pepper and Tabasco to taste, blending until incorporated.

recipes.name: CRÊPES SUZETTE
instructions: In 12-inch sauté pan, over medium heat, bring butter, orange juice, maple crystals, lemon juice, and zest to boil. Cook until thickened, about 3-4 minutes and stir in Grand Marnier and brandy. Bring again to boil for 30 seconds. Transfer syrup to bowl and set aside.

In separate 10-inch sauté pan, over medium-low heat, pour in small ladle full of syrup and heat to simmer. Place one crêpe (browned side down) in pan. Coat crêpe in warmed syrup then flip crêpe over with tongs to coat other side. Fold crêpe in quarters (fold in half then half again) to form triangle.
Pour 1 tablespoon of Grand Marnier per crêpe over top of folded crepe. Ignite by tilting pan toward burner. Allow alcohol to burn off before removing to plate and serving. Repeat to order.

recipes.name: CURRIED CHICKPEA CRÊPE FILLING

ingredients.name: vegetable stock or bean liquid from cooked chickpeas

instructions: In pressure cooker, combine chickpeas, water, cumin, salt, and bay leaves.
Bring pot to pressure, lower heat, and cook 30 minutes. Drain beans, set aside, and reserve bean liquid if using in place of stock.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add onions. Lower heat and cook until onions begin to soften and become translucent. Add curry. Cook 2-3 minutes more.
Add carrots and potatoes, stirring often to prevent sticking. Cook 5-6 minutes. Add garlic and salt. Cook 2-3 minutes more. Add stock or bean liquid reserved from chickpeas.

Add coconut milk and chickpeas. Simmer 3-4 minutes more. Add spinach. Cook until spinach becomes tender (about 1-2 minutes). Adjust seasonings. If mixture looks too thick, add bit more stock or bean liquid.

recipes.name: Flax Seed Drink
recipes.description: This drink contains phytoestrogens, omega-3 fatty acids, and is high in soluble fiber.
instructions: Grind flax seeds in spice grinder and mix with water. Drink immediately.

recipes.name: FRESH ALMOND MILK
instructions: In 2-gallon pot, bring water to boil, pour over blanched almonds and let sit covered for 20-30 minutes.
Transfer almonds and water to Vitamix. Blend until well homogenized.
Pour almond mixture in batches through sieve or chinois lined with double layer of rinsed cheesecloth, wringing and squeezing cheesecloth to extract as much liquid from pulp as possible.

recipes.name: Fried Tempeh (for Tempeh Reuben Sandwich)
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine marinade ingredients. Cover pan, bring to boil.
Add tempeh slices, lower heat, and simmer uncovered 30-40 minutes.
Drain tempeh and pat dry.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Brown tempeh slices on both sides. Drain on paper towel.

recipes.name: FRITTATA
instructions: In medium bowl whisk together filling(s), salt, and pepper with eggs.
Heat oil in sauté pan.
Pour in egg mixture.
Cook over medium-low heat until bottom is set.
Slide pan under preheated broiler for 1 or 2 minutes until lightly browned and set or, in alternative, transfer pan to 400°F oven for approximately 5 minutes.

recipes.name: GINGERBREAD MUFFINS
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare miniature muffin tins with muffin papers. Place muffin tins on sheet pan and set aside.
In small saucepan, on low flame, heat and whisk together butter, molasses, and corn syrup until mixed and butter is melted. Add ginger juice and set aside.
In medium bowl, sift together flour, sugars, ground ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Use whisk to incorporate ingredients.
Pour melted butter, molasses, corn syrup, and ginger juice into bowl with sifted dry ingredients. Stir to combine.
Pour batter into electric mixer, add eggs, and beat at medium speed for 1 1/2-2 minutes.
Using small ice cream scoop, fill muffin papers half way. Bake 10-12 minutes. Gently remove from pan. Cool completely.

recipes.name: GLUTEN-FREE AND VEGAN WAFFLES

ingredients.name: small amount of oil to brush or spray onto waffle iron

instructions: Pre-heat waffle iron.
In large bowl whisk together flours, baking powder, salt, maple crystals, and cinnamon.
In separate bowl, whisk oil, vanilla extract, and almond milk.
Make well in center of dry ingredients. Pour in liquid ingredients and whisk to combine.
In stand mixer, beat aqua faba until stiff peaks are achieved; fold into batter until barely blended.
Lightly grease waffle iron. For each waffle pour about 1/2-3/4 cup batter onto griddle.
Cook about 5-6 minutes per batch (longer cooking than egg waffles).

recipes.name: GOAT CHEESE, BEET, AND WALNUT SALAD
instructions: In large bowl, toss all greens together and put on individual plates.
Assemble each plate with endive, onion, beets, walnuts, goat cheese, and baguettes.
Dress each salad immediately prior to service.

recipes.name: GOLDEN TURMERIC MILK
instructions: In 2 batches, puree almonds, turmeric, and ginger with water in Vitamix until smooth. Strain milk through chinois.
Transfer milk to 1-gallon pot. Bring milk mixture to simmer over medium flame (to infuse flavors). Turn off heat and add pepper, cinnamon, and maple syrup to taste.

recipes.name: GREEN JUICE
instructions: Cut produce to fit juicer feed tube. Juice produce in order of ingredient listing, ending with celery stalks.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Hemp Coconut 'Milk' (for Golden Turmeric 'Panna Cotta')
instructions: Add hemp seeds, coconut milk, water, and salt to a high-speed blender.
Blend mixture until smooth, and strain through fine mesh strainer (or nut milk bag), if finer texture is desired.
Serve warm or cold, or use in your favorite recipes. Store in refrigerator in an airtight container for 3 to 5 days.

recipes.name: Hemp Seed Milk
instructions: Put all ingredients into high-speed blender and blend until smooth.
Serve milk chilled or warmed.

recipes.name: KASHA VARNISHKES (KASHA WITH BOWTIES)
instructions: Melt butter or oil in 10-inch sauté pan. Over medium-high heat, cook onions and mushrooms until caramelized, adding garlic toward end of cooking. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to large bowl.
In large pot of boiling salted water, cook pasta until al dente. Drain pasta and toss with onion mixture.
In small bowl, beat egg and add kasha. Stir until grains are well coated.
Wipe out sauté pan and heat again over high heat. Transfer kasha mixture to pan and cook, stirring, until grains are toasted and separate, 2 to 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and add stock. Stir, cover, and simmer until stock is absorbed and kasha is tender but not mushy, 7 to 8 minutes.
Stir in pasta mixture. Taste and adjust seasonings. Garnish with parsley and salmon.

recipes.name: Lemon-Cayenne Tea
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and drink in morning 1/2 hour before breakfast.

recipes.name: MANGO SAUCE (FOR CHICKPEA CRÊPE)
instructions: In blender, combine mango, tomatoes, tomato juices, shallot, canola oil, lime juice, and salt. Blend until creamy.
Adjust seasonings. Garnish sauce with jalapeño and cilantro.

recipes.name: Master Cleanse
recipes.description: Popularized by Stanley Burroughs (From Elson M. Haas, MD, The Detox Diet)
instructions: Mix and drink 8-12 glasses throughout day.
Eat or drink nothing else except water, laxative herb tea, and peppermint or chamomile teas.
Keep master cleanse in glass jar, not in plastic.
Rinse your mouth with water after each glass to prevent lemon juice from damaging enamel of your teeth.

recipes.name: Morning Glory Muffins
recipes.description: (Vegan)
instructions: Heat oven to 350° F (325° F in convection). Prepare muffin tins with paper liners.
Sift flour, sugar, baking soda, and cinnamon into bowl. Whisk ingredients together and set aside.
Combine carrot, raisins, pecans, coconut, and apple in bowl. Mix into the dry ingredients.
Whisk together the flax mixture, kuzu mixture, oil, and vanilla.
Add the liquid ingredients to batter. Stir to combine. Let batter sit for 2-3 minutes to allow moisture from the fruit to loosen batter, stir again.
Line muffin tin with cupcake liners. Portion batter with 1/4 cup ice cream scoop (yellow handle).
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until skewer or toothpick inserted in center of muffin comes out clean. Cool muffins completely on cooling rack before serving.

recipes.name: ORANGE, KIWI, AND RED GRAPE COMPOTE
instructions: In small saucepan, combine water, rice syrup, maple syrup, crushed cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and allspice. Whisk together and bring to boil. Reduce until mixture becomes thick and syrupy, about 3-4 minutes.
Add vanilla extract and vodka (if using) and continue to cook another 2 minutes. Remove from heat and remove cardamom pods and cinnamon stick.
In medium bowl, combine oranges, kiwis, and grapes. Combine syrup mixture with fruit and stir gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasonings, adding lime juice as needed.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 36 hours to allow flavors to combine. When ready to serve, sprinkle with toasted almonds.

recipes.name: PLAIN CRÊPES (CLASSIC)
instructions: In mixing bowl, sift flour with salt. Make well in center of dry ingredients. Break eggs into well and whisk until thoroughly incorporated. Immediately add 2 cups of milk, melted butter and brandy or rum (if using). Whisk together until incorporated.
Strain mixture through fine chinois to remove any lumps. Add more milk, if necessary, to achieve consistency of thin cream.
Refrigerate mixture for 30 minutes.

In 7-inch crêpe pan, fry crêpes. If storing, layer with parchment paper and wrap tightly so they do not dry out. If using immediately, pile cooked crêpes on plate, one on top of the other to keep them moist.

recipes.name: REAL BUTTERMILK WAFFLES
instructions: Heat waffle iron.
In large bowl, mix together flour, baking powder, salt, and maple crystals.
In separate bowl whisk egg yolks, butter, and buttermilk.
Mix wet ingredients with dry until batter is smooth. Set aside.
Beat eggs whites until soft peaks form. Fold egg whites into mixed batter.
Using 2 or 3-ounce ladle, pour batter onto waffle iron and cook 5-6 minutes, or until crispy.

recipes.name: RICE FLOUR GRIDDLE CAKES
recipes.description: (Gluten-Free, Vegan)
instructions: Whisk together flour, baking powder, maple crystals, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and ground flax seed.
In blender combine almond milk, and butter or oil.
Combine liquid ingredients and dry ingredients.
Using 1-ounce ladle, pour batter onto griddle. Cook cakes until bubbles in batter break on surface; flip and cook until browned.

recipes.name: RICH ALMOND MILK
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, bring water to boil. Add almonds and remove pot from flame. Let sit covered for 20-30 minutes.
Transfer almonds and water to Vitamix. Process for few minutes until well homogenized.
Strain milk through nut bag or chinois lined with 2 layers of moistened cheesecloth. Reserve almond pulp and set aside.
Add vanilla and salt. Whisk to combine.
Note: Save any pulp from almond milk for Nut Pulp Crisps recipe.

recipes.name: RICH ALMOND MILK (FOR ALMOND-FRUIT TART)
instructions: Combine almonds and water in blender or Vitamix. Process for a few minutes until well-homogenized.
Rinse piece of cheesecloth (double thickness) with cold water and wring thoroughly.

Pour small amount of almond mixture through sieve or chinois lined with prepared cheesecloth, wringing and squeezing cheesecloth to extract as much liquid from pulp as possible. Discard each batch of almond pulp when no more liquid can be extracted. Rinse cheesecloth well in cold water and proceed with next batch, repeating this process until all of almond mixture has been 'milked.'
Strain almond milk through sieve. Add vanilla.
Note: For even richer milk, soak blanched almonds in water for 20-30 minutes before blending.

recipes.name: SCRAMBLED EGGS
instructions: Collect equipment and food items: stainless steel bowl, whisk, spatula, sauté pan, eggs, salt, pepper, milk or cream, and butter.
Break eggs into stainless steel bowl and beat until well blended. Season with salt and white pepper. Do not use aluminum, which may discolor eggs.

If desired, add small amount of milk or cream, about 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons for 2 eggs, or 8 to 12 ounces per quart of eggs. Too much liquid may make cooked eggs watery and dilutes flavor. Heavy cream adds richness.
Heat butter in small sauté pan.
When fat is just hot enough to make drop of water sizzle, pour in eggs.

Cook over low heat, stirring gently with spatula from time to time as eggs coagulate. Lift portions of coagulated egg so that uncooked egg can run underneath. Too much stirring breaks up eggs into very small particles. Do not let eggs brown. Keep heat low.
When eggs are set but still soft and moist, remove from heat. Turn out onto plate or into steam table pan.

Additions to scrambled eggs: Flavor variations may be created by adding any of the following ingredients to scrambled eggs before serving: chopped parsley and/or other herbs; organic grated cheese (Cheddar, Swiss, parmesan); sautéed, diced onion and/or green pepper; diced smoked salmon.

recipes.name: SHERRY VINAIGRETTE
instructions: In medium mixing bowl, combine garlic, mustard, vinegar, salt, and maple syrup. Gradually whisk in olive oil.

recipes.name: Spelt Bread (for Tempeh Reuben Sandwich)
instructions: In small bowl, combine water and maple syrup then gently sprinkle yeast on top. Allow to sit until foamy.
Stir in oil, some of the flour, and salt until well combined. Gradually add more flour while stirring until dough is firm and workable.

Turn out dough onto lightly floured surface and knead to form sturdy and pliable dough. Transfer to large, lightly oiled bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let rise in warm place until doubled in size (about 1 hour).

Fold and turn dough, and rise again (about 30 minutes). Divide into two balls. Shape dough and transfer to lightly oiled loaf pans, score if desired. Cover with damp towels and rise again in warm place (about 20 minutes).
While bread is rising, pre-heat oven to 375° F. Bake bread until well-browned and finished (inner temp of 200° F). Remove from pan and cool on racks before slicing.

recipes.name: SPINACH-SHIITAKE SALAD
instructions: Heat oil over medium flame in 12-inch sauté pan. Add mushrooms and salt, and sauté until mushrooms are crispy and golden brown, stirring often to prevent sticking. There should be approximately 1 1/2 cups of cooked mushrooms.
Wash and dry spinach thoroughly. Transfer to large bowl and toss with mushrooms, pine nuts and onion.
Mix salad with dressing and top with 'Cheese Medallions.' Serve immediately.

recipes.name: SWEET BREW WITH CITRUS FRUIT
instructions: In 1-gallon pot, bring water to boil.
Turn off flame. Steep tea bags and fruit in water, covered, for 5 minutes.
Add apple juice to pot, stir and serve.

recipes.name: SWEET POTATO WAFFLES
instructions: Heat waffle iron.
In large bowl, whisk together sweet potatoes, egg yolks, milk and butter.
In separate bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, cornmeal, salt, baking powder, and maple crystals.
Mix wet ingredients into dry until batter is smooth. Set aside.
Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Fold egg whites into mixed batter.
Using 2 or 3-ounce ladle, pour batter onto waffle iron and cook 5-6 minutes, or until crispy.

recipes.name: SWEET VEGAN CRÊPES
instructions: Combine all ingredients in blender. Let batter sit for 30 minutes in refrigerator.

recipes.name: Tempeh Reuben Sandwich
instructions: Fried Tempeh (recipe follows):
In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine marinade ingredients. Cover pan, bring to boil.
Add tempeh slices, lower heat, and simmer uncovered 30-40 minutes.
Drain tempeh and pat dry.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Brown tempeh slices on both sides. Drain on paper towel.
Spelt Bread (recipe follows):
In small bowl, combine water and maple syrup then gently sprinkle yeast on top. Allow to sit until foamy.
Stir in oil, some of the flour, and salt until well combined. Gradually add more flour while stirring until dough is firm and workable.

Turn out dough onto lightly floured surface and knead to form sturdy and pliable dough. Transfer to large, lightly oiled bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let rise in warm place until doubled in size (about 1 hour).

Fold and turn dough, and rise again (about 30 minutes). Divide into two balls. Shape dough and transfer to lightly oiled loaf pans, score if desired. Cover with damp towels and rise again in warm place (about 20 minutes).
While bread is rising, pre-heat oven to 375° F. Bake bread until well-browned and finished (inner temp of 200° F). Remove from pan and cool on racks before slicing.
Ketchup (recipe below):
In blender, combine raisins (with soaking liquid), tomato puree, garlic, water, paprika, cayenne, cinnamon, and salt. Blend until all ingredients are combined.
In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, on high heat, heat oil. Slowly add tomato mixture. Lower heat and simmer 40 minutes. Add Worcestershire sauce and lemon juice. Simmer 5 minutes more. Adjust seasonings.

recipes.name: Tofu Scramble
instructions: In 12-inch sauté pan over medium heat, warm oil. Add onion and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in garlic, pine nuts, cumin, red pepper flakes and turmeric; sauté 2 minutes more.
Add mashed tofu, tomato, salt and lime juice to pan. Raise heat and simmer, stirring, for 5 minutes to heat through.

recipes.name: Vegan and Gluten-Free Spiced Fruit Muffins
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Line muffin tins with muffin papers or use silicon baking molds.
Whisk together almond meal, flax meal, ground quinoa, oats, baking powder, salt, pepper, spices, and orange zest in bowl; set aside.
Whisk together applesauce, oil, and maple syrup in separate bowl.
Make well in dry ingredients and pour in wet mixture; stir to combine. Mix in pear and cranberries (or apples and blueberries).
Fill each muffin chamber 2/3 full. Bake 20-25 minutes or until skewer inserted in center of a muffin comes out clean.
Leave muffins in chambers for 10 minutes before inverting onto a cooling rack. Allow muffins to cool completely before serving.

recipes.name: Watermelon Juice
instructions: Cut watermelon into approximately 2 inch x 4 inch pieces.
In a high-speed blender puree watermelon pieces in batches.
Using a mesh strainer set over a large bowl strain watermelon juice. Discard solids.
Stir in lemon juice and refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.name: WILD RICE PANCAKES
instructions: In large bowl, whisk together flour, maple crystals, baking powder, soda and salt.
Roughly chop cooked rice (needs to be dry, fluffy before adding to batter) and mix with dry ingredients.
In separate bowl, whisk together milk and lemon juice. Let stand 15 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons of oil or butter.
Gradually add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and stir to combine. Whisk egg whites to stiff peaks and fold into combined ingredients.
Heat griddle or large non-stick pan over medium heat. Brush little of remaining tablespoon of oil over surface of pan.
Using 1-ounce ladle, pour batter onto griddle. Cook cakes until bubbles in batter break on surface; flip and cook until browned.

recipes.name: Pomegranate, Blueberry, and Ginger Elixir
recipes.description: A vibrant, antioxidant-rich tonic balancing the earthy sweetness of dark berries with the fiery, kinetic bite of fresh ginger. This intensely restorative elixir promotes energetic circulation and grounds the body while stimulating the senses.
instructions: Combine pomegranate juice, blueberries, ginger juice, and agave in VitaMix and puree. Do not strain. Serve over ice.

recipes.name: Cucumber Agua Fresca
recipes.description: A deeply refreshing, cooling elixir that harnesses the watery essence of cucumber and the bright, volatile acidity of lime to soothe the spirit. Perfect for intense summer heat, this beverage restores thermodynamic equilibrium through its cooling properties.
instructions: Combine cucumbers, lime juice, mint, water, and agave in blender and puree until smooth.
Strain puree through sieve and serve in glasses with slice of lime.

recipes.name: Hibiscus-Mint Cooler
recipes.description: A visually striking, ruby-red infusion uniting the tart, fiery nature of hibiscus flowers with the crisp, ethereal cooling effect of fresh mint. This harmonizing cooler acts as a powerful botanical reset during transitional seasons.
instructions: Combine water and hibiscus tea in stockpot. Bring to boil, turn off tea, and steep for 20 minutes. Chill tea in ice bath.
Combine agave and mint leaves in suribachi with 2 cups of cooled tea. Muddle (crush) mint leaves with agave and tea using surikogi (pestle) until well combined.
Add mint mixture to remaining tea and strain.
Serve over ice and garnish with mint sprig.

recipes.name: ALMOND-FRUIT TART WITH ALMOND CRUST
recipes.description: (Wheat-Free)
instructions: For pastry cream: Combine agar, water and maple syrup in 2 1/2 quart saucepan. Soak agar 10 minutes.
Bring agar mixture to boil, lower heat and simmer with lid slightly ajar until agar is dissolved, about 15 minutes. Whisk or stir often, scraping agar from sides and bottom of saucepan.
Stir almond milk, salt, and extracts into agar mixture. Bring to boil, whisking often.
Add kuzu slurry, whisking vigorously, until mixture comes back to boil. Cook few minutes longer.
Pour mixture into shallow pan and chill in freezer or refrigerator until set.
In food processor, whip chilled mixture until very smooth and creamy. Halfway through processing, stop machine and scrape sides of work bowl with spatula.
For tart assembly: Fill tart crusts with Almond Pastry Cream. Arrange fruit on top of cream.

recipes.name: Almond Fruit Torte
recipes.description: (Spring/Summer)
instructions: Oil and flour 8 1/2 inch spring form pan.
Powder almonds in food processor. Add eggs, 1/2 cup maple syrup, and almond extract. Process until smooth. Pour batter into pan.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes. Top should be firm to touch and brown. Do not remove cake from pan.
In one-quart saucepan, soften agar flakes in water for 10 minutes. Cook covered, stirring often until agar is dissolved.
In separate pot, combine strawberries with 1/4 cup maple syrup and cook over medium flame, covered, until soft. Puree in blender, and put through sieve to remove seeds.
Add strawberry puree to agar mixture, stirring well. Add dissolved kuzu to pot stirring constantly until thick and clear and mixture comes to boil.
Adjust sweetness with remaining maple syrup, if desired.
Let strawberry mixture cool slightly. Pour over cake before removing sides of spring-form pan.
Let mixture set, then remove sides of spring-form pan.
Garnish with kiwis and oranges and serve.

recipes.name: ALMOND PASTRY CREAM
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine agar, water, and maple syrup. Let mixture sit for 10 minutes.

Bring agar mixture to boil. Lower heat and simmer uncovered or with pan lid slightly ajar until agar is dissolved, about 15 minutes. Stir often, scraping agar from sides and bottom of saucepan with spoon. Whisk mixture as necessary to break up bits of un-dissolved agar.
Stir almond milk, salt, and vanilla extract into agar mixture. Bring to boil, whisking often.
Lower heat and add kuzu slurry, whisking vigorously until mixture comes back to simmer. Cook a few minutes longer.
Pour mixture into hotel pan and chill in freezer or refrigerator until set.

In food processor, puree chilled mixture until very smooth and creamy. Halfway through processing, stop machine and scrape sides of work bowl with rubber spatula. If sweeter cream is desired, add additional maple syrup to taste.
Chill almond cream thoroughly, if thicker texture is desired.

recipes.name: Almond Pulp Cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Combine all ingredients in bowl with spatula.
Form cookies on parchment-lined 1/2 sheet pan with 1-ounce scoop.
Bake cookies 10-12 minutes, or until lightly golden.

recipes.name: Almond Torte
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil and flour 8-inch spring form pan.
Powder almonds in food processor. Add eggs, maple syrup and almond extract. Process until smooth.
Pour batter into pan.
Bake for 40 minutes. Top should be firm to touch and golden brown.

recipes.name: AMARETTI COOKIES
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 325°F. Line 2 half-sheet pans with Silpats.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks; add maple crystals one tablespoon at a time and continue whipping until incorporated.
Add extracts and salt; whip 10 seconds more.
Using rubber spatula, fold almond flour into egg white mixture. Mixture will be soft and 'meringue-like' in consistency.
Scoop dough onto sheet tray with 1-ounce ice cream scoop. Top each cookie with 8-10 pignoli nuts.
Bake 18-20 minutes or until cookies are golden. Cool cookies before carefully removing from pan with metal offset spatula.

recipes.name: APPLE CRUMB PIE
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Roll out pie dough and line pie plate. Trim and form edges, cover, and chill for at least 30 minutes.

In small bowl, whisk together flours. In separate bowl, whisk together oil and maple syrup. Slowly drizzle oil and maple syrup mixture into flour mixture. Stir lightly to form small, moist crumbs. Cover and chill.
In 10-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add apple slices and sauté until apples are slightly softened. Set aside to partially cool.
In large bowl, combine apples, maple syrup, lemon juice, vanilla, spices, salt, and flour. Toss until apples are well coated.
Place filling in pie shell. Top with crumbs. Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake pie for 40-45 minutes or until apples are tender and crust is firm. Remove foil 10 minutes before removing pie from oven.
Cool pie before serving.

recipes.name: APPLE-OAT CRUMBLE
recipes.description: (FALL/WINTER)
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350°F. While cutting apples, soak slices in acidulated water (juice of 1/2 lemon and 4 cups water).
In large bowl, whisk together salt, arrowroot, cinnamon, maple crystals, and apple juice. Drain apples, and combine with cinnamon-maple mixture. Transfer to 9-inch square pan.
In medium bowl combine oats, flour, and cinnamon. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl whisk oil, syrup, and salt.
Pour wet into over dry and toss until mixture is completely coated.
Spread topping over apples. Bake 45 to 55 minutes until topping is golden and apples and filling is bubbly. Serve garnished with drizzle of pomegranate reduction.

recipes.name: Apple Phyllo Roll
instructions: Preheat conventional oven to 400°F (convection oven will dry phyllo too much).
Prepare large bowl of water and add lemon juice. Peel, core, and thinly slice apples to 1/8-inch thickness and transfer them to lemon water to prevent browning.

Drain apples in colander. In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add apples, coconut sugar, and cinnamon. Sauté apples on medium heat until they release most of their moisture and become tender, stirring frequently. Transfer apples to bowl to cool.

Unroll phyllo on work surface and cover with damp cloth. To assemble, lay one sheet of phyllo on parchment paper horizontally. Brush sheet with oil and sprinkle lightly with small amount of walnuts. Repeat process, stacking and brushing another 3 sheets.

Spoon apple mixture horizontally along bottom of phyllo, leaving 1-inch border on bottom and 2 inches on left and right side. Fold in left and right sides over filling, then roll phyllo from bottom to top to form log. Repeat steps 5-7 for the second phyllo roll.
Score both rolls halfway through on bias into 8 equal portions. Brush roll with remaining oil.
Transfer rolls to parchment-lined sheet tray and bake for 30-35 minutes or until golden.
Cool ten minutes, then slice all the way through pre-scored cuts. Serve with Lemon and Maple-Flavored Yogurt (recipe below).

recipes.name: APPLE RING
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. In large bowl, combine yeast, water, apple juice, rice syrup, and 2 cups all-purpose flour; stir until smooth. Cover sponge and set aside in warm place for 30-45 minutes.
Add melted oil, salt, and maple crystals. Mix together all-purpose and whole wheat pastry flours. Add flour, cup-by-cup until dough is formed that pulls away from sides of bowl.
Knead dough on table about 10-15 minutes, using remaining flour until smooth dough forms.

Transfer dough to large, clean, lightly oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Proof in warm place for 45-60 minutes or until dough has doubled in size. While dough is proofing, prepare two half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Turn/fold dough. Rise one more time.

Divide into two equal portions. Roll out first dough into rectangle about 1/4” thick. Pull edges of dough to create a rectangular shape. Spread half of apple filling across near end of dough horizontally. Fold dough over filling and roll log forward until seam is on bottom. Attach ends of dough to create ring. Move ring to prepared baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Loosely cover rings with damp towel and set aside in warm place. Rise until dough has doubled in size, about 15-20 minutes. Cut 5-6 slits (steam vents) in top of each ring. Glaze each ring with maple syrup.
Transfer bread to oven and bake approximately 30-45 minutes or until dough is thoroughly browned. Cool rings completely before serving.

recipes.name: APRICOT PARFAIT
instructions: In 1-gallon pot, combine juice, agar flakes and vanilla extract. Let sit for 10 minutes to help agar dissolve.
Bring mixture to boil, and reduce to simmer, covered, until agar is completely dissolved, stirring and scraping bottom and sides of pot with wooden spoon to avoid sticking.
Pour juice mixture into hotel pan to cool quickly. Once steam has stopped rising, place in refrigerator to set up and harden into kanten.
Blend 3/4 kanten briefly in processor. Pour in serving bowls.
Blend remaining 1/4 kanten briefly with cashew butter. Serve as topping. Garnish with almonds and mint leaf.

recipes.name: Avocado and Coconut Terrine
instructions: Avocado layer: Blend avocados, lime juice, salt, coconut milk, coconut cream, and agave syrup in Vitamix until creamy.

Transfer mixture to ice cream machine and freeze until scoop-able consistency is achieved. Transfer mixture to half hotel pan and freeze for 20 minutes or until mixture firms to scoop-able consistency.
Coconut layer: In medium bowl, whisk together coconut milk, salt, vanilla extract, coconut extract, and maple syrup.
Transfer to ice cream machine and freeze until scoop-able consistency is achieved. Transfer to half hotel pan and freeze until mixture firms to scoop-able consistency.

Brush terrine mold lightly with oil and line with parchment paper. Spread avocado sorbet evenly in bottom of terrine mold. Swirl in coconut sorbet. Smooth surface of terrine and transfer to freezer to set until firm.

recipes.name: Baked Custard (Crème Caramel)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In large bowl, combine eggs, maple crystals, salt and vanilla.
In small saucepan, scald milk (heat to just below simmering), then slowly whisk into egg mixture.
Strain mixture through chinois and skim foam from surface.
Set 6 ramekins in water bath reaching halfway up their sides. Add enough caramel* to cover bottom of ramekin. Carefully pour in custard.
Bake approximately 60-90 minutes. Water should be almost simmering as custard cooks. Do not let it boil as this makes the custard grainy.

To test for doneness, insert thin-bladed knife about an inch or two from the center. Custard is done if knife comes out clean. Center may not be completely set, but it will continue to cook in its own heat after removal from the oven.
Chill completely and un-mold right before service.

Crème Caramel: In small saucepan, simmer 1 cup maple crystals and 1/4 cup water, swirling to dissolve sugar until mixture caramelizes. Cover pan and boil over medium heat until bubbles are thick. Line bottoms of ramekins with hot caramel, tilting to spread evenly.

recipes.name: Baked Meringue Shells
instructions: Preheat oven to 225°F and line sheet tray with parchment paper.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks, then add sweetener one tablespoon at a time until incorporated and meringue is stiff.
Using pastry bag or spoon, pipe or spoon meringue on sheet tray. Bake until crisp (minimum 2 hours).
Cool shells completely and remove from parchment.

recipes.name: BANANA CAKE
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottom of pans with parchment.
In medium bowl, sift together dry ingredients. Whisk to combine.
In food processor, combine wet ingredient and process until smooth.
Using rubber spatula, transfer wet ingredients from food processor to bowl with dry ingredients. Mix to combine.
Pour batter into two prepared pans. Bake about 20-25 minutes or until top are golden brown, and cakes are springy to touch.
Cool on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: BANANA CUPCAKES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare miniature muffin tins with cupcake liners.
Cream butter and sugar together in stand mixer until light and fluffy. Add egg and mashed banana, mixing thoroughly.
Sift and whisk dry ingredients together in bowl; add to butter and egg mixture in mixer.
Whisk to combine milk, vinegar, and vanilla; add mixture to batter in mixer.
Fill cupcake liners using ice cream scoop, filling 2/3 full. Top with slice of banana.
Cook for 15-20 minutes. Check doneness by with toothpick in center (should come out clean).

recipes.name: Basil Ice Cream
instructions: Prepare ice bath. Bring water to boil. Add salt. Blanch basil for 2-3 seconds then shock in ice bath. Drain basil and completely wring water from it.
Combine coconut milk, maple syrup, rice syrup, vanilla extract, lemon zest, salt and basil in blender.
Process mixture until well emulsified.
Pour mixture into ice cream machine and churn until creamy and somewhat firm.

recipes.name: BERRIES AND CREAM TERRINE
instructions: For vanilla layer: In a high-speed blender, combine soaked cashews, coconut milk, agave syrup, coconut oil, vanilla extract, lemon juice, scraped vanilla bean and sea salt.
Blend on high for a few minutes until mixture is completely smooth.
Transfer filling into rectangular 6 x 4-inch silicone molds, filling them halfway up (approximately 1 cup per mold) and place in the freezer.
For blueberry layer: Add frozen blueberries, coconut milk and agave syrup into a small saucepan.
Bring mixture to a simmer over high heat. Reduce for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until mixture is reduced to 1 1/2 cups. Cool over ice bath.
Pour cooled mixture into high-speed blender. Add soaked cashews, coconut oil, lemon juice, and salt.
Blend on high for a few minutes until the mixture is completely smooth.
Gently spoon mixture on top of vanilla layer already setting in silicone molds.
Freeze for one hour, or until firm.
To serve: Let terrines sit for 5 to 10 minutes at room temperature before serving.
Place terrines on a serving plate. Top with cut blackberries and mint.
Store any leftover terrines in the freezer.

recipes.name: BERRY-GRAPE KANTEN
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine grape juice and agar flakes. Soak agar for 5 minutes.
Bring agar-juice mixture to boil over medium heat, whisking frequently. Lower flame and simmer 5 minutes or until agar is completely dissolved.
Add ginger juice, lemon zest, and agave syrup to juice mixture. Simmer 2 minutes more.
Divide and arrange grapes and strawberries equally among individual ramekins.
Slowly pour juice mixture over grapes and strawberries in ramekins. Let mixture stand until no more steam rises. Transfer kanten to refrigerator until firmed up, about 30 minutes.
Serve kanten as is from ramekins.

recipes.name: Berry Sorbet
instructions: In blender, puree berries with grape juice, vodka, and lime juice.
Strain puree through fine sieve to remove seeds. Add maple syrup to taste.
Transfer berry mixture to ice cream machine and process until frozen.

recipes.name: Big Chewy Oatmeal-Raisin Cookies
instructions: Heat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare 2 half sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, beat butter with sugars until creamy, approximately 3 minutes. Beat in egg.
Separately whisk flour, salt, baking powder, and nutmeg together. Add dry ingredients into butter-sugar mixture. Stir in oats and optional raisins.
Form dough into 24 (1-inch) balls using 1-ounce scoop, placing each cookie every 2 inches apart on sheet trays.
Bake until cookie edges turn golden brown, 20 to 25 minutes. Halfway during baking, rotate trays front to back and switch them from top to bottom.
Slide cookies cooling rack and let cool at least 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: BLACK AND WHITE COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection). Line 2 half-sheet pans with parchment paper.
Whisk together flours, baking powder, salt and lemon zest in bowl and set aside.
Beat eggs and sugar in bowl until smoothly blended. Add milk, butter, and vanilla extract.
Slowly add egg/sugar mixture into flour mixture, blending until smooth.
Using 1-ounce scoop, drop cookies 2 inches apart on sheet tray. Bake for about 15 minutes, until lightly golden and tops feel firm to touch.
Remove cookies to wire racks and cool at room temperature before frosting.
Whisk confectioner's sugar in bowl with 2-3 tablespoons boiling water until thick but smooth.

Remove frosting from heat and reserve 3 tablespoons of frosting to make 'black' frosting; use remainder to frost half of each cookie (if frosting becomes too thick, add drops of boiling water again until it is spreadable).
Melt chocolate in small bowl over simmering water. Stir in corn syrup.

Add reserved white frosting to chocolate and stir to spreadable consistency (adding more hot water, if necessary, to thin). Spread bare half of each cookie with chocolate frosting. Set cookies aside until frostings set.

recipes.name: BLACK SESAME SEED ICE CREAM
instructions: Prepare ice bath. Combine coconut milk, maple syrup, rice syrup, salt, and sesame seeds in pot over high heat. When mixture boils, turn heat down and whisk for 1-2 minutes. Remove mixture from heat, and transfer pot to ice bath to cool mixture to room temperature.
Pour mixture into ice cream machine and churn until creamy and somewhat firm.

recipes.name: Blueberry Sauce
instructions: Combine blueberries, apple juice, and maple syrup in pot. Bring mixture to simmer.
Simmer sauce uncovered until blueberries begin to pop open and sauce begins to thicken, approximately 15 minutes.
Stir in lemon zest and vanilla. Simmer another minute.

recipes.name: BUTTER CRUST
instructions: Sift then mix flour and salt into bowl. Using two knives or pastry cutter, cut butter into flour to form very coarse meal.
With rubber spatula, lightly toss flour while sprinkling water in mixture 1 tablespoon at a time until dough forms. Wrap in plastic and chill 20 to 30 minutes.
Roll on lightly floured parchment to desired shape.

recipes.name: CARAMEL
instructions: Combine all ingredients in sauté pan. Bring sauce to simmer and cook uncovered for 10-12 minutes until sauce is reduced and thick enough to coat back of spoon. Remove from heat and let cool completely.

recipes.name: Caramelized Apples
instructions: Melt butter or oil in large 12-inch pan over medium heat. Add apples to the pan with cinnamon, ginger, and salt.
Sauté apples until caramelized, stirring only occasionally, approximately 15 minutes.
Add maple syrup to pan. Sauté apples another 5-10 minutes until mixture thickens.

recipes.name: CARAMELIZED ONION TART
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter or oil 9-inch tart pan with removable bottom.
Roll crust between parchment; chill for 15 minutes. Transfer crust to prepared pan and rest in fridge again for 30 minutes more.
Heat butter or oil in 12-inch sauté pan over medium/low heat. Add onions and cook over (stirring occasionally) until caramelized, about 20 minutes.
While onions cook, half blind bake tart crust (with pie weights) for approximately 10-12 minutes (or until lightly golden).
Remove crust from oven; turn temperature down to 335°F.
Spread caramelized onions into tart shell (do not pat down).
Whisk together custard ingredients and pour over onions.
Bake until custard is set and crust is golden brown, approximately 12-15 minutes.

recipes.name: CAROB CAKE WITH WALNUTS
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil and flour one 8-inch cake pan and line bottom with parchment.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared baking pan.
Sprinkle walnuts on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.

recipes.name: Carrot Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare miniature muffin tins with muffin papers.
Whisk dry ingredients together in large bowl.
Whisk together wet ingredients. Add raisins and walnuts.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and mix. Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, fill muffin papers 2/3 full and bake for 25-30 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

recipes.name: CHECKERBOARD COOKIES
instructions: For vanilla dough: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, beat together butter, maple crystals, and salt until light and fluffy with paddle attachment. Add egg and vanilla and continue to mix until well combined.

Whisk together flour and baking powder in separate small bowl. Add flour mixture to butter mixture in mixer until combined. Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate 10 minutes to firm up while making chocolate dough.
For chocolate dough: In stand mixer, beat together butter, maple crystals, and salt until well combined. Add egg, baking powder, and almond extract. Continue to mix until smooth.

Whisk together flour and cocoa powder in separate small bowl. Gradually sift flour/cocoa mixture into butter mixture and mix just until combined. Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate at least 10 minutes until firm.
For assembly: Divide vanilla dough into 5 equal pieces. Divide chocolate dough into 4 equal pieces.

On parchment, using flour as necessary for dusting, roll out each piece dough to 1/4 inch. Make 3 stacks of rolled dough, brushing each layer with egg white: 1) vanilla/chocolate/vanilla; 2) chocolate/vanilla/chocolate; 3) vanilla/chocolate/vanilla.

Using bench scraper, square off sides of each stack of dough. Freeze 3 stacks of dough until hard. Using sharp knife, cut lengthwise rectangles of each dough, brush them with egg white, and stack rectangles in same order as listed above. Cut crosswise at 1/4 inch intervals across rectangle stacks to form cookies. Trimmed scraps of dough can be bundled together and re-rolled, frozen and stamped with cookie cutter shapes to make marbleized cookies.
Transfer to sheet trays. Brush tops with egg white. Bake 6-10 minutes or until golden at edges. Remove from pans to racks to cool.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE-ALMOND GANACHE
instructions: Place chocolate in medium bowl.
In 2 1/2 quart pot, bring almond milk to boil and pour over chocolate, whisking vigorously, until chocolate melts and mixture is smooth.
Let ganache cool to room temperature.
Beat with stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment for several minutes, until ganache becomes lighter and somewhat thicker.
Chill ganache in refrigerator until it acquires spreadable consistency.
Variation: Add 1/4 to 1 teaspoon flavored extract to finished ganache.

recipes.name: Chocolate Bark

ingredients.name: sprinkle of coarsely ground sea salt

instructions: Line half-sheet pan with parchment paper. Prepare ice bath in small bowl. Have offset spatula and candy thermometer at the ready.
Bring 4 cups water to simmer in 2-quart pot.

Pour 1 1/2 cups ground chocolate in small bowl. Set bowl over simmering water and whisk chocolate until completely melted. Remove bowl from heat and take temperature of melted chocolate. Temperature should not exceed 125°F. Between 110 and 125°F is best.
When chocolate is in 110 and 125°F range, whisk in remaining 1/2 cup of ground chocolate. Cool chocolate to 85°F, transferring bowl to ice bath, if necessary.

Transfer bowl atop simmering water again, and whisk chocolate until it reaches temperature between 87 and 91°F degrees (be careful as temperature rises quickly). If temperature goes too high, again use ice bath to cool it quickly.
Pour chocolate on parchment-lined half-sheet pan. Spread with offset spatula to 1/8-inch thickness.
Sprinkle nuts, dried fruit, cacao nibs, and salt over surface.
Cool bark in refrigerator and break into pieces.

recipes.name: Chocolate Biscotti
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line one half-sheet tray with parchment paper.
In small double boiler, melt chocolate chips. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
In bowl whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
Using stand mixer, mix butter, maple crystals, and melted chocolate. Add egg whites. Blend one minute more. Scrape sides of bowl with spatula and blend another thirty seconds.
Add dry ingredients (flour, cocoa, baking soda, salt) to mixer to combine. Dough will very sticky. Divide dough in two.
Roll each dough in chopped nuts and then form each into log shape on sheet tray (6 inches apart). Flatten logs into length of about 8 1/2 inches and width of 3 inches.
Bake 20 minutes or until firm to touch. Remove from oven, lower heat to 300° F, let logs cool 10-12 minutes.
Using bread knife, slice logs into 1/4 inch to 1/2 inch diagonal slices.
Cook slices 7-10 minutes more on each side. Cool and serve. (These get crunchier as they sit.)

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE CHERRY PECAN BARS
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil, flour, and parchment line 9-inch by 9-inch square baking pan.

In stand mixer, beat butter, date sugar, maple crystals, and vanilla until fluffy. In bowl, whisk together all-purpose and whole wheat pastry flours. Slowly sift flours into butter mixture until combined.
Press dough in even layer in prepared pan. Bake for about 10 minutes (rotate pan half way through cooking to ensure even baking) or until edges are lightly browned. Set aside to cool.
In stand mixer, beat date sugar, maple crystals, flour, salt, vanilla, and eggs until smooth. Stir in pecans, cherries, orange zest, and chocolate chips and mix just to combine.
Spread filling over crust to create even layer. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until edges are golden brown and filling is set.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes before unmolding onto cooling rack. Transfer to freezer to cool completely before cutting into bars.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Line 2 sheet trays with parchment paper.
Cream together butter, brown sugar, and white sugar in stand mixer, until sugars are completed incorporated and mixture is light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla. Mix to incorporate.
In separate bowl, sift together flour, baking soda and salt.
Add flour mixture to butter/sugar/egg mixture in 1/2 cup increments until flour is completely incorporated. Fold in chocolate chips.
Using 1-ounce scoop, drop cookies onto baking sheet at 2-inch intervals.
Cook 10-12 minutes or until golden at edges. Let cool.

recipes.name: Chocolate Coating (for Truffles)
instructions: Create double boiler: Fill 1-gallon pot with 4 cups water. Bring water to simmer. Cover pot with heatproof bowl. Combine 1 1/3 cups chocolate and coconut oil in bowl and stir until chocolate is completely melted and smooth.
Immediately remove bowl from pot and wipe moisture from bottom of bowl with dry towel. Stir in remaining 2/3 cup chocolate until chocolate is again smooth.
Using slotted spoon, dip truffles one by one into melted chocolate. Let excess chocolate drip off.
Transfer covered truffle to parchment-lined sheet pan. Sprinkle with garnish (crushed pistachios, toasted coconut, or lime zest/sea salt).
Repeat process with remaining truffles. Refrigerate until chocolate coating has set.

recipes.name: Chocolate Fondue
instructions: In small saucepan, combine cocoa, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and orange extract, stirring until well combined.
Cover pot and gently bring to simmer. Lower heat and cook for 1-2 minutes, being careful not to burn chocolate.
Remove from heat and stir in soy milk until sauce has nappé.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE GELATO
instructions: Prepare ice bath.
In 1-gallon pot, heat milk, heavy cream, and 3/4 cup of maple crystals until crystals dissolve and milk starts to simmer.
Whisk in cocoa powder and bittersweet chocolate. Set aside.
Combine egg yolks and remaining 3/4 cup of maple crystals in electric mixer fitted with paddle attachment. Beat on high speed for 3-5 minutes or until mixtures lightens in color and mixture thickens.
Lower speed on mixer and slowly pour chocolate-cream mixture into egg mixture.
Transfer combined mixtures to 2 1/2 quart saucepan and simmer over low heat stirring constantly until thickened (candy thermometer should read at about 180 degrees). Do not bring mixture to boil.
Strain mixture into medium bowl through nut bag or chinois lined with double layer of moistened cheesecloth, and then stir in Kahlua, vanilla, and salt.
Transfer mixture to ice bath and cool to room temperature.
Pour mixture into ice cream machine and churn until firm and scoop-able.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE-PEANUT BUTTER FROSTING
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk and agar powder. Set aside for at least 5 minutes.
Prepare ice bath.
In food processor, combine coconut cream, peanut butter, maple crystals, cocoa powder, and salt. Blend until smooth.
Bring coconut milk-agar mixture to boil. Simmer until agar powder has dissolved, stirring constantly to avoid scorching.
Slowly and carefully add coconut milk-agar mixture and melted chocolate to processor with other ingredients and process to combine.
Using spatula, transfer contents from food processor to small bowl over ice bath until chilled.

recipes.name: Chocolate Sauce
instructions: In double boiler (bowl set over simmering water), melt chocolate.
In separate pot, bring almond milk to simmer, and turn off heat.
Slowly whisk just enough almond milk into melted chocolate to create a smooth and pourable sauce.

recipes.name: CHOCOLATE SOUFFLÉ
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Butter inside of soufflé dish (or dishes) with the one tablespoon of softened butter.
Dust inside of each dish with cocoa powder.
Refrigerate dishes until ready to fill.
Melt chocolate and remaining 4 tablespoons butter in medium bowl set over pot of simmering water. Turn off heat, stir in salt and vanilla and set aside.
In separate medium bowl, beat egg yolks and maple crystals with whisk or hand mixer until thick and yellow (about 3 minutes). Pour into chocolate mixture.
In separate medium bowl or electric stand mixer, combine egg whites and cream of tartar. By hand or mixer, whip egg whites until stiff, moist peaks are formed.
Vigorously stir one-quarter of whites into chocolate-egg yolk mixture.
Gently fold in remaining egg whites in 4 equal increments.
Transfer to ramekins and bake as follows: 1/2 cup dishes: 12 to 14 minutes, 2 cup dishes: 20 to 25 minutes, 1 quart dishes: 30 - 35 minutes, 2 quart dishes: 50 to 55 minutes.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: COCONUT-LIME CREAM TART
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Oil 9-inch tart pan with removable bottom.

Using your fingertips, blend together flour, macadamias, shredded coconut, maple crystals, salt and coconut oil until mixture resembles coarse meal. Press mixture into tart pan. Refrigerate for 15-20 minutes. Bake for 10-15 minutes or until golden brown. Set aside to cool.

Combine coconut milk into 2 1/2 quart saucepan with agar flakes, rum, maple syrup, brown rice syrup and salt. Bring to boil over medium heat, lower heat and simmer (whisking occasionally) about 30 minutes or until agar is completely dissolved.

In second 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine semolina flour and cold water. Over high flame, whisk constantly until mixture thickens (consistency should resemble thick cream of wheat). Turn off heat and whisk into coconut milk mixture. Add lime juice and zest. Whisk to combine.
Pour filling into large bowl to cool, stirring constantly, to prevent mixture from setting up. When filling is warm (not hot), pour into cooled tart shell. Garnish with toasted coconut and lime zest.

recipes.name: COCONUT-LIME FLAN
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk and agar. Soak agar for 5 minutes.
Bring mixture to boil. Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for about 5 minutes or more, until agar is completely dissolved.
Add maple syrup and stir until combined.
Dissolve kuzu in lime juice and water until there are no lumps. Add to milk mixture and simmer until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Lightly oil ramekins and sprinkle 2 teaspoons maple crystals in bottom of each ramekin.
Pour custard into ramekins. Refrigerate to set.
When custard is set, run paring knife around the side of each ramekin to separate custard. Invert custard onto plate. Garnish with coconut.

recipes.name: COCONUT MACAROONS
instructions: Preheat oven to 325° F. Line 2 half-sheet pans with parchment and lightly oil or use Silpats.

In 2 ½ quart pot, combine maple crystals, water, and salt. Bring to boil and reduce to simmer. Cook until mixture thickens and reaches softball stage (about 20-25 minutes/234-240°F). Soft ball stage is reached when small droplet of syrup poured into ice water and forms soft, pliable ball. Remove from heat, cover mixture, and set aside to cool to about 155°F before combining with beaten eggs.
Combine egg whites and vanilla in medium bowl and beat with whisk by hand to form stiff peaks.
Very gradually, fold beaten egg whites into slightly cooled syrup mixture just until combined. Carefully fold in pulsed coconut. Refrigerate dough 10-15 minutes to let set before scooping.

Form cookies with 1-ounce scoop, rounding each into a ball, and then rolling them in crushed pistachios. Transfer cookies to lightly oiled, parchment lined baking sheets. Bake for 15-20 minutes or until firm and bottoms of cookies are slightly golden.

recipes.name: COFFEE CUSTARD
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine milk and agar. Soak agar 5 minutes.
Bring mixture to boil, lower heat, and simmer uncovered for about 5 minutes or more, until agar is completely dissolved.
Add maple syrup and stir until combined.
Dissolve kuzu and coffee in water until there are no lumps. Add to milk mixture and simmer until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Lightly oil ramekins and sprinkle 2 teaspoons maple crystals in bottom of each ramekin.
Pour custard into ramekins. Refrigerate to set.
When custard is set, run paring knife around side of each ramekin to separate custard. Invert custard onto plate. Garnish with pecans.

recipes.name: COFFEE GRANITA
recipes.description: (SPRING/SUMMER)
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart sauce pan, bring water to boil. Add instant coffee and maple crystals and stir until coffee and maple crystals are dissolved. Add Kahlua and salt. Whisk to combine and remove from heat.
Pour mixture into half hotel pan (mixture should be about 1/4 inch up side of pan) and transfer to freezer for about 1 hour.
Remove pan from freezer and use fork to scrape any ice crystals that have formed on side or bottom of pan. Return to freezer and repeat scraping every 30 minutes for 3-4 hours.
Once mixture is thoroughly frozen, scrape once more with fork, returning granita to “dry” in freezer for another half hour before serving.

recipes.name: CORNMEAL CRUST
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Combine cornmeal, pecans, and oats in food processor. Grind to fine meal.

Whisk together oil, maple syrup, and sea salt. Add wet ingredients to dry in processor until cookie-like dough is formed. Press dough into lightly oiled tart pan. Bake tart 12-15 minutes or until firm and lightly browned. Cool.

recipes.name: CRANBERRY PEAR PIE
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Roll out first pie dough and line pie plate. After dough rests in refrigerator for 15 minutes, trim edges, cover, and chill for at least 30 minutes more. Roll out second dough and cut into 1/2 inch x 10 inch strips. Transfer strips to baking sheet, cover, and chill until ready to use.
In 2 1/2 quart sauce pan, combine cranberries, syrup, and orange juice. Bring to boil and reduce to simmer for 5 minutes or until all cranberries have popped. Add pears or apples.
Stir in arrowroot slurry and cook until mixture loses chalky appearance and thickens, about 1 minute. Transfer mixture to bowl to cool.
Spoon cooled filling into chilled pie shell. Arrange lattice strips on top. Trim ends of strips flush with overhang of shell and form edge.
Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Remove foil from edges 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool and set pie before serving (at least 30 minutes).

recipes.name: CRANBERRY WALNUT SCONES

ingredients.name: almond milk soured with 1 tablespoon lemon juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line half-sheet pan with parchment.
In medium bowl, stir together flours, maple crystals, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
With pastry cutter, cut butter into dry ingredients until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add cranberries, nuts, and zest.
Make well in center and gradually stir in milk, ginger juice, and maple syrup just to combine. Do not over mix; dough should be sticky and difficult to work with.
On lightly floured surface, pat or roll dough to 1/2 inch thickness. Cut into shapes and place on sheet pan. Brush tops with milk and sprinkle with maple crystals.
Bake 12-15 minutes or until golden brown and firm to touch. Remove from pan to cool.

recipes.name: CREAM CHEESE FROSTING

ingredients.name: eight-ounce packages of organic cream cheese

instructions: In stand mixer, on low speed, beat cream cheese with butter until smooth.
Gradually beat in maple crystals, vanilla extract, and salt until well blended.
Chill to set up.

recipes.name: Crème Anglaise (Stirred Custard)
instructions: Heat cream or milk and vanilla to scalding (just below simmering) in double boiler.

In medium bowl, beat together egg yolks and maple crystals. Slowly pour hot cream/milk into egg mixture while whisking constantly (this raises the temperature of the eggs gradually and helps prevent curdling).

Heat mixture slowly in double boiler, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Sauce is cooked when it lightly coats the back of a spoon instead of running off like milk, or when it reaches 185°F. Never let the temperatures go above 190°F.
When done, remove sauce from heat. Cool sauce by setting pan or bowl in ice water. Stir occasionally to cool evenly.
Note: If sauce accidentally curdles, it is sometimes possible to save it. Immediately stir in 1-2 tablespoons cold milk, transfer sauce to blender, and process at high speed.

recipes.name: CURRANT SCONES
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350° F.
Sift and whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and maple crystals.
Cut butter into dry mix to form coarse crumbs.
In another bowl, beat egg, heavy cream, zest and currants together.
Add wet to dry until just combined.
Fold out onto table and form semi-flattened log.
Cut log into triangles and bake on parchment for 10 minutes.
Serve warm.
Note: If using rice flour add more liquid (about 2 tablespoons).

recipes.name: Flourless Chocolate Cake

ingredients.name: boiling water mixed 1 heaping tablespoon instant coffee

instructions: Heat convection oven to 325°F. Brush 9-inch spring-form pan with oil. Line bottom with parchment paper and outside, bottom of pan with tin foil.
Grind chocolate in food processor to fine meal, add date sugar, and continue to grind until well combined.
Slowly pour hot coffee into food processor through feeder tube and pulse until chocolate is melted.
Add butter pieces and cocoa powder. Pulse to combine. Add eggs, salt, and vanilla. Process until smooth. Batter should be pourable and creamy.
Pour batter into spring-form pan. Bake on half-sheet pan as a little batter may seep out.
Bake about 45 minutes or until puffed and lightly cracked. Use toothpick to check for doneness.

recipes.name: Flourless Coconut Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F. Brush 8-inch cake pan with oil and line with parchment.

In Kitchen Aid, whip coconut sugar and egg yolks about 5 minutes or until ribbons form. Add dried coconut and salt and carefully mix to combine. Remove bowl with egg yolks and coconut sugar from Kitchen Aid and set aside.
Fit Kitchen Aid with new, clean bowl. Whip egg whites until stiff peaks form. Using rubber spatula, carefully fold egg whites into other bowl with sugar and egg yolks. Transfer batter to cake pan.
Bake about 30 minutes or until cake is golden and set in middle.

recipes.name: FRENCH VANILLA ICE CREAM
instructions: Prepare ice bath.

In 2-quart saucepan, combine milk, 1/4 cup of maple syrup, sea salt, vanilla pulp, and vanilla pod. Whisk mixture to combine. Heat mixture on medium flame over flame tamer, stirring occasionally, until temperature reaches 175°F. Remove from heat.

While milk mixture is warming, combine remaining 1/4 cup maple syrup, rice syrup, egg yolk, and vanilla extract in medium-sized bowl. Beat with electric hand mixer until contents turn pale yellow and form semi-thick ribbons (about 5 minutes).

Slowly and gradually whisk 1/2 cup of hot milk mixture into beaten egg mixture, being careful not to cook yolks. Then carefully whisk milk and egg combination back into pot with remaining milk mixture. Heat over medium flame, stirring constantly, until temperature reaches 180°F (remove from heat to accurately take temperature).
Remove vanilla pod. Strain mixture into non-reactive bowl. Whisk in heavy cream.
Cool mixture in ice bath. Pour mixture into ice cream machine and freeze to scoop-able consistency.

recipes.name: FRENCH WALNUT TART

ingredients.name: arrowroot dissolved in 2 tablespoons cold water

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Roll out first dough and transfer to tart pan; chill for 15 minutes. Trim edges of rolled dough, allowing 1-inch overhang. Cover and chill for 30 minutes more. Roll out other half of dough and transfer to sheet pan. Cover and chill until ready to use.
In one-gallon pot, combine sweeteners. Bring to boil, lower heat and add lemon juice, salt, almond milk, and walnuts.
Whisk in nut butter, extracts, and brandy. Add arrowroot slurry. Mix on medium low heat until mixture thickens slightly. Remove from heat and cool.
Pour walnut mixture into tart shell. Place top dough over filling, trim and seal edges. Cut a few steam vents.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until crust is firm and golden.
Cool before serving (about 25 minutes).
Note: If cashew butter is very thick, loosen it up with 1-2 tablespoons of water or nut milk.

recipes.name: FRESH BERRY TART WITH NUT CRUST
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil 9-inch tart pan or use 5-6 four-inch, non-stick paper tart pans.
In food processor, grind pecans to fine meal with flour, maple crystals, baking powder, and salt.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil and maple syrup.
Add oil and syrup to dry ingredients in processor. Pulse lightly until dough comes together.
Press crust mixture into tart pan(s). Refrigerate 15-20 minutes, then bake 20-25 minutes. Let cool completely.
In small pot, simmer agar flakes in apple juice until agar completely dissolves. Add kuzu/juice slurry. Whisk until mixture thickens. Add maple syrup, pinch of salt, and berries.
Cook 6-8 minutes. Remove from heat and let mixture cool partially. Pour filling into cooled crust.
Let set completely. Garnish with mint before serving. There may be filling left over. Puree in food processor to make pudding.

recipes.name: Fresh Strawberries and Bananas
instructions: In bowl, toss strawberries with maple crystals. Set aside to macerate for 30 minutes.
In separate bowl, combine bananas with lemon juice. When strawberries are done macerating, add bananas to strawberries.

recipes.name: Fudgy Chocolate Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil one 8-inch cake pan. Dust pan with 2 teaspoons of cocoa powder. Line bottom of pan with parchment paper.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Add finely chopped chocolate and mix to combine. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 35-40 minutes until cake is springy to touch and pulls away from sides.
Cool in pan on wire rack 10-15 minutes. Remove from pan and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: GENOISE
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with lightly buttered or oiled parchment.

Add eggs, coconut sugar, and vanilla to stand mixer bowl and beat at high speed for about 6-10 minutes until mixture has tripled in volume and has become light in color and foamy. Mixture should be almost consistency of stiff peaks.
Gently transfer egg mixture into clean large bowl. Sift flour in small batches (3 times) into egg mixture while folding batter with large rubber spatula.
Divide batter into 2 prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes or until cake is golden brown and springy to touch.
Using paring knife, cut cake away from sides of pan immediately, leaving cake in pans to cool for 10 minutes.
Remove cakes from pans, remove parchment from bottoms of cakes, and cool completely on wire racks. Use cakes as two layers or split each of them and use as four layers.

recipes.name: GHIRARDELLI AWARD WINNING CHOCOLATE BROWNIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F (325° F in convection oven). Grease and flour 8 x 8-inch square baking pan and line with parchment paper.
Whisk eggs with sugar and vanilla; add melted butter.
Whisk together dry ingredients (cocoa, flour, baking powder, and salt) and fold into egg mixture. Add nuts.
Bake for 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in middle of brownie comes out clean.

recipes.name: GINGER CAKE
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
Place softened butter in bowl of stand mixer. On low speed, mix just until butter is fluffy. Add sea salt and maple crystals; mix until creamy and well combined, about 2 minutes.

Add one egg at a time. Slowly add in maple syrup, orange juice, milk, and extracts. Combine on medium speed until well incorporated (mixture may look curdled, but will come back together once remaining ingredients are added).
Spoon combined dry ingredients into mixer a little at a time and mix until completely incorporated into butter mixture, scraping down sides of bowl as necessary.
Pour batter into 2 prepared pans. Bake about 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown and springy to touch.
Cool on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: GLUTEN-FREE CHOCOLATE CAKE
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease 9 1/2-inch Bundt pan with butter and dust with cocoa powder.
In food processor, blend dates with maple syrup.
When dates are thoroughly blended, add vanilla, eggs and melted butter. Mix to combine.
In medium bowl, sift together flours, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Whisk well to incorporate. Add to date-syrup mixture in food processor. Mix to combine.
Pour batter into baking pan, filling no more than 2/3 up side of cake pan. Any extra cake batter can be used for muffins. Do not overfill pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes. Allow cake to cool completely.
Double-melt chocolate and drizzle over cake. Sprinkle with walnuts.

recipes.name: Gluten-Free Chocolate Chip Cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F. Line 2 half-sheet pans with parchment paper.
In medium bowl whisk sorghum flour, buckwheat flour, tapioca starch flour, brown rice flour, white sweet rice flour, and baking powder together. Set aside.
Cream butter and maple crystals with paddle attachment in stand mixer.
Add egg, vanilla, and salt to butter/maple crystal mixture, and salt. Beat on slow speed for 30-60 seconds more.
Stop mixer and add flour mixture to other ingredients. Mix to combine. (Mixture will be stickier than type of “drop” batter prepared with wheat flour.) Add chocolate chips.
Using 1-ounce scoop, portion dough onto baking sheets. Place approximately dozen cookies per sheet with good distance between, as cookies spread.
Cook for about 7-10 minutes or until cookies are nicely golden (do not under-bake).
Transfer to racks until cooled and firmed up.

recipes.name: GLUTEN-FREE CHOCOLATE MACAROONS
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line half sheet tray with parchment paper.
Melt chocolate in double boiler, and set aside to cool.
In medium bowl, add salt to egg whites and beat with hand mixer or whisk to soft peaks. Slowly add maple crystals, spoonful by spoonful, to form until incorporated.
Using spatula, fold in vanilla and coconut.
