Fold in cocoa powder and cooled melted chocolate. Gently fold to incorporate all ingredients.
Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, transfer cookie dough to sheet tray, leaving space between for slight spread.
Bake 15-20 minutes. Cool and serve.

recipes.name: GLUTEN-FREE CRISP GINGER COOKIE
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F. Line 3 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
In medium bowl whisk almond meal, sorghum flour, arrowroot flour, ground ginger, and black pepper.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, water, and salt.
Pour syrup mixture into nut/flour mixture. Batter should be consistency of heavy cream. If it is too thick, add more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you have proper consistency.

Using teaspoon measure, drop batter onto sheets (5-6 cookies a sheet). Decorate each cookie with one sliced almond. Bake 15-20 minutes or until cookies are golden. Cool before removing from sheet pan.
Note: Cookies hold shape better on Silpat.

recipes.name: GLUTEN-FREE SWEET POTATO PECAN TART

ingredients.name: gluten free breadcrumbs mixed with 2 tablespoons maple crystals
whole pecans or 1 cup thick coconut flakes

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and lightly grease tart pan with small amount of softened butter or oil.

Grind pecans and maple crystals to fine meal in food processor. Add flours and pulse to combine about 30 seconds more. Transfer mixture from food processor to bowl. In separate bowl, whisk together melted butter, water and, salt. Pour wet mixture into dry and mix to combine. If mixture is too moist, refrigerate for 5-10 minutes before pressing out crust.
Press crust mixture into tart pan. Refrigerate 15-20 minutes or until crust is firm to touch. Pierce crust with fork and partially bake for 15-20 minutes. Cool before filling.
Before filling tart shell, sprinkle breadcrumbs and maple crystals over crust (this prevents crust from getting soggy).
In food processor, puree yams. Add syrup, eggs, cream, vanilla, ginger juice, ground spices, and salt. Blend until mixture is creamy and smooth. Transfer puree to partially baked pie shell.
Decorate top of tart with pecans and brush nuts with maple syrup or top with coconut (omitting maple syrup wash).
Bake tart 30-35 minutes until filling is just firm. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Golden Turmeric 'Panna Cotta' with Ginger-Pepper Lace Cookies
instructions: Grease inside of small silicone molds with oil.

Combine agar flakes and milk in medium saucepan and simmer over medium heat until agar flakes have dissolved. Add cardamom, turmeric, ginger, maple syrup, vanilla bean, and salt. Simmer an additional 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Strain mixture through chinois and pour into silicone molds. Cool until firm.
In blender, puree blackberries and maple syrup. Strain coulis and transfer to squeeze bottle.
Preheat convection oven to 300°F. Line 5 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
Transfer pecans to medium bowl. Add flour and arrowroot. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl, whisk oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, ginger, black pepper, and salt. Add to pecan/flour mixture, mixing until combined. Let batter sit for 15 minutes.
Use teaspoon to drop batter onto Silpat-lined baking sheets. Place only 5 cookies per sheet – one in each corner and one in middle. Bake one sheet at a time for 10 minutes until cookies are bubbly.

Cool cookies for approximately 30 seconds before removing from Silpats. Working quickly (because cookies cool and set hard very fast), remove tuiles from sheet tray using small offset spatula and wrap around cannoli molds. Repeat procedure with remaining sheet trays until all batter is used.
Invert panna cotta onto plate. Garnish with tuile, blackberries, gold dust, blackberry coulis and mint sprigs.

recipes.name: GRAPEFRUIT-CAMPARI GRANITA
recipes.description: (FALL/WINTER)
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, over low flame, simmer juice with water and maple crystals until maple crystals dissolve. Add Campari and stir.
Pour mixture into half hotel pan (mixture should be 1/4 inch up side of pan) and transfer to freezer for about 1 hour.
Remove pan from freezer and use fork to scrape any ice crystals that have formed on side or bottom of pan. Return to freezer and repeat scraping every 30 minutes for 3-4 hours.
Once mixture is thoroughly frozen, scrape once more with fork, returning granita to “dry” in freezer for another half hour before serving.

recipes.name: GREEN APPLE SORBET
recipes.description: (FALL/WINTER)
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot over medium flame, simmer thyme leaves, agave, water, and salt for 15 minutes.
Remove pot from flame. Pour mixture into blender and puree to combine. Strain and set aside in medium bowl.
In separate bowl, combine juiced lemons with agave-thyme mixture.
Juice apples in Champion juicer and combine with lemon juice and agave-thyme mixture.
Transfer mixture to ice cream machines and freeze until scoop-able consistency is achieved. Transfer sorbet to 9-pan and freeze forty minutes to one hour or until sorbet firms up.

recipes.name: HAZELNUT-MOCHA AND ALMOND PARFAIT
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine water, espresso, almond milk, and agar flakes. Let mixture sit 10 minutes or more. Over high heat, bring mixture to boil. Lower heat and simmer uncovered or with pan lid slightly ajar until agar is dissolved, scraping sides and bottom of pan often with spoon.
Add maple syrup, salt, vanilla extract, and chocolate chips, whisking until smooth. Simmer a few minutes longer.
Pour mixture into hotel pan and transfer to freezer or refrigerator until set.
Puree mixture with hazelnut butter in food processor until very smooth. Stop machine several times and scrape sides of work bowl with rubber spatula. Chill puree thoroughly.
To serve, spoon into glasses, alternating with Almond Pastry Cream (recipe preceding) and garnish with hazelnuts.

recipes.name: JAM DOT COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Grind almonds, flour, oats, and cinnamon in food processor to fine meal.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil, maple syrup, and sea salt. Add liquid to dry mixture in food processor and mix until well combined.

Form cookies using level 1-ounce scoop. Round them into walnut sized balls. Place on baking sheet and form indentation in middle of cookie using floured ¼ teaspoon measure. Fill indentation with about ½ teaspoon of jam and bake 15-20 minutes or until golden.

recipes.name: KABOCHA SQUASH PIE
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Place squash cut side down on parchment-lined half sheet pan and bake until fork tender, approximately 1 hour.
Discard squash seeds and pulp (or save seeds for toasting). Scoop and reserve 2 cups of squash from its skin for this recipe.
Prepare an ice bath.

Puree squash, maple crystals, spices, and salt in food processor until smooth. Transfer mixture to 2 1/2 quart pot and slowly whisk in milk and cream. Simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens, about 3-5 minutes. Remove pot from heat and place in ice bath for 10 minutes before slowly whisking in eggs.
Pour filling into pie shell and bake for 30-40 minutes or until filling is lightly cracked around edges and center jiggles slightly. Cool for 1 hour before slicing.

recipes.name: KANTEN
instructions: Soak agar flakes in juice for 10 minutes in 2 1/2 quart saucepan.
Bring mixture to boil. Watch carefully to prevent liquid from boiling over. Reduce heat to simmer and cook until agar is completely dissolved, whisking frequently.
Place sliced strawberries in an 8-inch square baking dish.
Slowly pour agar and juice mixture over berries. Set aside until no steam is rising from mixture.
Place in refrigerator until firmed up, about 45 minutes. Can either be served cut into cubes or blended in food processor for 'pudding.'

recipes.name: Lemon Soy Cream Frosting
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine juice, agar flakes, and salt. Let sit for 5 minutes. Simmer mixture until agar is fully dissolved, about 10 minutes.
In food processor, puree tofu with maple crystals until very creamy. Add maple syrup, oil, and extracts, and process until very smooth.
Slowly, with processor running, drizzle hot juice-agar mixture into tofu mixture. Fold in zest.
Transfer frosting to medium bowl and refrigerate to set up.

recipes.name: LEMON WAFER COOKIES
recipes.description: (Gluten-Free)
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350°F. Line 2 sheet trays with parchment paper.
In food processor, grind almonds to fine meal with flours, baking soda, and salt.
In separate smaller bowl, whisk together wet ingredients.
Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients in processor (mixture will be loose). Chill dough in refrigerator for 10-15 minutes.
Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, scoop batter onto sheet tray, leaving room between each cookie as batter spreads.
Sprinkle each cookie with few almond slices.
Cook 15 minutes or until cookies are slightly golden. Cool before removing from parchment paper.

recipes.name: LEMON WHIPPED COCONUT CREAM
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk, agar, and coconut cream. Set aside for at least 5 minutes.
Prepare ice bath. Bring coconut mixture to simmer constantly stirring until all the agar is dissolved.
In Vitamix, combine coconut mixture, agave syrup, lemon zest, lemon juice, and salt. Blend until smooth. Slowly add coconut butter and blend to combine.
Transfer to bowl and set over ice bath until chilled.
Process frosting in food processor until smooth.

recipes.name: LIGHT LEMON TART

ingredients.name: apple juice or white grape juice

instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, simmer agar in apple juice until agar is completely dissolved.
Add rice syrup, maple syrup, turmeric and pinch of salt.
Combine kuzu slurry with vanilla; add to agar-juice mixture. Cook until kuzu begins to thicken and goes from cloudy to clear.
Add lemon juice and zest.
Pour mixture into shallow bowl or pan and cool completely. Whisk frequently so that it does not 'set up.'
When mixture is cooled, pour into pre-baked and cooled tart crust.
Refrigerate tart to set filling.
Note: There may be lemon filling left after filling tart. Let it set totally and blend it in food processor for creamy smooth pudding.

recipes.name: Lime-Sea Salt Chocolate Ganache Truffles
instructions: Bring coconut milk, 1/4 tsp lime zest, and 1/4 tsp salt to simmer in 2-quart pot.
Remove coconut milk from heat. Add chocolate. Stir with spatula until smooth.
Pour chocolate mixture into shallow baking pan and chill in freezer for 30 minutes, or until firm enough to scoop.
Form 1-inch diameter truffles using small half-ounce scoop or teaspoon.
Return truffles to freezer to firm.
Dip truffles in Chocolate Coating (recipe following) and garnish with lime zest and sea salt. Serve truffles at room temperature.

recipes.name: Meringue Frosting
instructions: In medium bowl, whisk egg whites, agave, vinegar, salt, and cream of tartar. Place bowl over 2 1/2 quart pot of boiling water. Make sure water underneath bowl is rapidly boiling.
Whisk mixture for about 10 minutes (mixture will become white and frothy).
Remove from heat and add vanilla extract.
Using hand mixer, whip at medium-high speed until light and fluffy, about 4-5 minutes.
Note: If doubling recipe, frosting can be whipped in stand mixer.

recipes.name: Mint-Chocolate Ganache Truffles
instructions: Bring coconut milk and salt to simmer in 2-quart pot.
Remove coconut milk from heat. Add chocolate and mint extract. Stir with spatula until smooth.
Pour chocolate mixture into shallow baking pan and chill in freezer for 30 minutes, or until firm enough to scoop.
Form 1-inch diameter truffles using small half-ounce scoop or teaspoon.
Return truffles to freezer to firm.
Dip truffles in Chocolate Coating (recipe following). Serve truffles at room temperature.

recipes.name: Mocha Frosting
instructions: Prepare coffee by combining instant coffee, salt, and boiling water. Set aside.
In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk, prepared coffee, agar powder, and coconut cream. Set aside for 5 minutes.
Bring coconut milk-coffee mixture to boil. Lower heat and simmer until all agar powder has dissolved. Transfer to ice bath.
In food processor combine cashew butter and maple crystals. Add coconut-coffee mixture. Blend well until smooth.
Add melted chocolate and mix to combine. Transfer mixture to small bowl.
Place bowl over ice bath until mixture is firm.
Blend frosting in food processor until smooth and pipe-able.

recipes.name: OLIVE OIL CRUST
instructions: In medium bowl, sift together flour, salt and baking powder.

Cut oil into flour mixture all at once but do not mix. Toss flour around lightly coating fat to create little balls of flour coated fat. A light touch is important here. Final blending will take place on pastry board in rolling.
Add just enough water (one tablespoon at a time) to form ball, being careful not over-mix and create too much gluten.
Flatten dough into disc, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate for 15 minutes to relax the dough. Roll to desired shape. Transfer rolled dough to pie or tart pan and chill for 30 minutes or more.
Heat oven to 375°F, fill crust and bake.

recipes.name: Orange Blossom Panna Cotta
instructions: In 1-gallon pot, combine heavy cream, maple syrup, and salt. Cook uncovered on low simmer, stirring constantly for about 5-7 minutes. Turn off heat and set aside.

Pour soaked agar and water mixture into separate 2 1/2 quart pot. Bring to boil, cover pot, lower heat, and simmer until all agar is completely dissolved, about 5 minutes. Add to pot with heavy cream mixture and cook 2-3 minutes longer. Add orange blossom water and orange zest.
Add buttermilk to heavy cream/agar mixture.
Ladle mixture into 4-ounce ramekins. Refrigerate until set.
Combine orange supreme with rice syrup and serve as garnish with nuts.

recipes.name: Orange Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pan.
Cool in pans on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: Orange Sorbet
instructions: In medium bowl, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, rice syrup, lemon juice, vodka, and sea salt.

Pour mixture into ice cream machine and freeze until scoop-able consistency is achieved. When mixture starts to firm up, add zest and continue to churn until incorporated. Transfer sorbet to freezer to firm consistency.

recipes.name: ORANGE WHIPPED COCONUT CREAM
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk and agar. Set aside for at least 5 minutes.
Prepare ice bath. In Vitamix, combine melted coconut cream, agave syrup, orange zest, orange juice, and salt. Blend until smooth. Slowly add coconut butter and blend to combine.
Bring coconut-agar mixture to simmer. Simmer until all agar powder has dissolved, stirring constantly to avoid scorching.
Slowly add boiling coconut-agar mixture to Vitamix with other ingredients and blend to combine.
Using spatula, transfer mixture to medium bowl and set over ice bath until chilled.
Process frosting in food processor until smooth.

recipes.name: PAN-FRIED POLENTA CAKES
instructions: Pour hot polenta onto parchment-lined half-sheet tray, and spread with lightly oiled spatula to 1/2 inch thickness. Let set until firm, 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Cut into desired shapes using cookie cutters.
Spread cornmeal on plate and dredge polenta. Prepare another plate with paper towel for draining.
Heat 1/4 inch oil in sauté pan, and fry polenta cakes over medium high heat until golden and crisp. Flip once and fry other side.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare 2 sheet trays with parchment paper.
Cream sugars and butter in stand mixer until light and fluffy.
Add egg, peanut butter, and vanilla to butter-sugar mixture.
Whisk together flour, salt, and soda and add to mixer until dough is smooth.
Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, place dough balls every 2 inches on half-sheet trays.
Press cookies flat with fork. Bake 15 minutes.

recipes.name: Pecan Tuiles

ingredients.name: melted coconut oil or canola oil

instructions: Preheat convection oven to 300° F (350° F in conventional oven). Line 5 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
Transfer chopped pecans to medium bowl and add flour and arrowroot. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl, whisk oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt until thoroughly combined. Add to pecan/flour mixture, mixing until combined. Let batter sit for 15 minutes.

Use teaspoon measure to drop batter onto Silpat-lined baking sheets. Place only 5 cookies per sheet – one in each corner and one in middle. Bake one sheet at a time for 10 minutes until cookies are bubbly.

Cool cookies for approximately 30 seconds before removing from Silpats. Working quickly (because cookies cool and set hard very fast), remove tuiles from sheet tray using small offset spatula and wrap around cannoli molds. Repeat procedure with remaining sheet trays until all batter is used.

recipes.name: PHYLLO CUPS WITH SAUTÉED APPLES

ingredients.name: sticks melted butter or 1 cup no taste oil

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F degrees. Oil muffin tins (3 tins, 6 muffins each).
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo, brushing each layer with either melted butter or oil. Sprinkle each layer with pinch of maple crystals and pinch of cinnamon.
Cut layered phyllo into six equal pieces, making six 4-inch by 4-inch squares. Repeat process until all phyllo is used.
When all 18 squares are complete, carefully press them into muffin tins. Bake for 7-10 minutes or until phyllo cups are golden.
Remove cups from tins and cool. Fill with sautéed apples (recipe following) and ice cream. Garnish plate with cinnamon, toasted nuts, and fresh mint.
Heat clarified butter in 8-inch sauté pan until hot. Add apples and brown 3-5 minutes. With slotted spoon, transfer apples to warm plate.
Pour off clarified butter and deglaze with juice, then add syrup and vanilla or rum. Reduce by little more than half, or until bubbles cover surface of pan.
Cool sauce for minute or two. Mount with cold butter.
Transfer apples to phyllo cup. Coat apples with 1 to 2 tablespoons of sauce and dust with cinnamon and nuts. Top with ice cream. Use remaining sauce as underliner for phyllo cups.

recipes.name: Phyllo Triangles with Feta and Kale
recipes.description: (Year-Round)
instructions: Heat convection oven to 350°F. Line half sheet tray with parchment. Set aside.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil over medium flame. Sweat onion, garlic, ½ teaspoon salt, nutmeg, and red pepper flakes until onions are translucent. Set aside.

In 2-gallon pot, bring 1 gallon water to boil with remaining 1 tablespoon salt. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch kale until tender, about 3-5 minutes. Shock in ice water and drain in colander. Squeeze excess moisture from kale and finely chop.
Return pan with onions to burner over medium flame and add kale. Sauté mixture until kale is heated through.
When mixture has cooled, transfer to medium bowl. Add feta and ricotta cheeses and mix to combine. Season to taste.
Unwrap phyllo and lay one sheet on parchment paper horizontally. Cover remaining sheets with damp towel. Brush phyllo with butter.

Spoon seven 1-tablespoon dollops of mixture across bottom edge of phyllo at equal distances. Cut phyllo into strips between each dollop, and fold up “flag” style (see diagram) to make triangular shape. Transfer finished phyllo triangles to prepared sheet pan. Brush tops with more butter. Repeat with remaining phyllo.
Just before baking, brush all triangles with butter again. Bake 20 minutes or until evenly golden.

recipes.name: Phyllo Triangles with Tofu and Spinach
recipes.description: (Year-Round)
instructions: Heat convection oven to 350°F. Line half sheet tray with parchment. Set aside.
Press tofu between paper towels on sheet pan with weighted plate for amount 30 minutes. Transfer tofu to medium bowl and crumble it with fingertips. Set aside.

In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil over medium flame. Sweat shallots, salt, fennel, cumin, and paprika until shallots are translucent. Transfer mixture to bowl with tofu. Add miso and umeboshi. Mix to combine. Chop spinach and combine with tofu mixture. Season to taste.
Unwrap phyllo and lay one sheet on parchment paper horizontally. Cover remaining sheets with damp towel. Brush phyllo with oil.

Spoon seven 1-tablespoon dollops of mixture across bottom edge of phyllo at equal distances. Cut phyllo into strips between each dollop, and fold up “flag” style (see diagram) to make triangular shape. Transfer finished phyllo triangles to prepared sheet pan. Brush tops with more oil. Repeat with remaining phyllo.
Just before baking, brush all triangles with butter again. Bake 20 minutes or until evenly golden.

recipes.name: POACHED PEAR TART WITH CORNMEAL CRUST
instructions: Poach pears in grape juice until fork tender. Transfer pears to plate and chill; reserve poaching liquid.

In 2 1/2 quart pot, simmer 1 1/2 cups poaching liquid with agar flakes until agar is dissolved. Stir in kuzu slurry and cook, stirring gently, until mixture turns clear. Remove from heat, cover with lid, and set aside.
Spread layer of raspberry jam in bottom of prepared crust. Arrange sliced or fanned pears on top of jam. Top with glaze. Chill until set (about 20 minutes).
In blender, puree raspberries and maple syrup. Strain out seeds and pour into squeeze bottles. Serve with tart.

recipes.name: POMEGRANATE GRANITA
recipes.description: (FALL/WINTER)
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, over low flame, simmer pomegranate and orange juices with maple crystals until crystals dissolve.
Pour mixture in half hotel pan (mixture should be 1/4 inch up side of pan) and transfer to freezer for about 1 hour.
Remove pan from freezer and use fork to scrape any ice crystals that have formed on side or bottom of pan. Return to freezer and repeat scraping every 30 minutes for 3-4 hours.
Once mixture is thoroughly frozen, scrape once more with fork, returning granita to 'dry' in freezer for another half hour before serving.

recipes.name: Raspberry Sauce (for Almond Fruit Tart)
instructions: Combine maple crystals and water in a pot and stir until dissolved.
Combine frozen raspberries and hot syrup in a food processor. Pulse a few times till pureed.

Pour puree through a fine mesh strainer set over a medium-size bowl. Stir and push on the solids with the back of a rubber spatula until all of the liquid has been extracted. This will take several minutes as the mixture will be thick.
Discard the seeds. Add the liqueur, if using, and stir to combine.

recipes.name: Raspberry Shortbread Linzer Cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line two half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, cream butter and maple crystals together until fluffy.

Whisk together flours and arrowroot in separate medium bowl. Slowly sift flour mixture into butter mixture while continuing to mix until well combined. Add cashews and continue to mix until incorporated. Divide dough equally into 2 and wrap each piece in plastic. Chill in refrigerator for 15-20 minutes, until dough firms.

Roll out both doughs to about 1/8” thickness. Freeze dough until hard. Cut dough with lightly floured cookie cutters. For each cookie, cut solid bottom and mate with center cut out using smaller cutter. Continue process until all dough is used.

Place cookies on 2 sheet trays (bottoms on one tray and tops with centers cut out on other). Bake about 5-6 minutes and rotate pans. Continue to bake until edges are lightly browned. Remove from pans and cool on racks.

When cool, spread 1 tablespoon preserves on solid cookie bottom. Lightly sprinkle cookie tops (with holes) with powdered sugar, if using. Carefully press top cookie with hole on jam-topped bottom. Continue process until all cookies are assembled.

recipes.name: RAW "CHEESECAKE"
instructions: Line 9-inch spring-form pan with parchment paper.
In food processor combine dates, pecans, coconut oil, and sea salt. Process until dough binds when pressed with fingers. Do not over-blend.
Press dough evenly into bottom of spring-form pan.
Freeze until crust is set, about 15 minutes.
Drain and rinse cashews, discarding soaking water.
In high-powered blender, puree cashews, coconut milk, agave nectar, coconut oil, lemon juice, vanilla bean, and salt. Blend until very smooth.
Decorate surface of cheesecake with droplets or lines of puree.
Using skewer or dinner knife, swirl mixture to create marbled effect.
Freeze cheesecake until solid.

recipes.name: RICE PUDDING
instructions: In 1-gallon pot, bring water, vanilla pulp and pod, cinnamon stick, and sea salt to boil. Add rice and cover. Reduce heat to low simmer and slowly cook, covered, until rice absorbs all water, about 30 minutes. Remove rice from heat and let rest, covered, without stirring, for 15 minutes. Rice should not be fully cooked, as it will continue to cook in almond milk mixture.

Add almond milk, maple crystals, maple syrup, and rice syrup. Simmer, uncovered, over medium heat about 30-40 minutes. Stir mixture often to release starch from rice. This will allow pudding to become thick and creamy. Occasionally taste for doneness and continue to cook accordingly.
Add currants, zest, and juice. Remove cinnamon stick, and transfer pudding to bowl to cool.
Chill pudding in refrigerator. Garnish with walnuts and cinnamon just before serving.

recipes.name: ROLLED FIG COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line two half-sheet trays with parchment paper and set aside.
In food processor, sift together flours, almond meal, and cinnamon. In small bowl, whisk together salt, syrup, and oil.
Add wet mixture to dry in food processor. Pulse to combine.
Divide dough evenly in half. Flatten dough into 2 discs and wrap each in plastic wrap. Refrigerate 10-15 minutes to firm.
In 2-quart pot, combine figs, apple juice, vanilla, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Simmer 5-7 minutes or until figs are softened. Drain figs, reserving cooking liquid.
Puree fig mixture in food processor, adding cooking liquid as necessary, to make smooth, spreadable paste. Set aside to cool.
Roll each dough separately on parchment paper (dough should be about 1/8 inch thick. Trim excess dough so that dough roughly measures 10” by 6” rectangle.

Spread cooled or room temperature filling over rolled out dough. Roll dough jelly roll style as tightly as possible. Wrap dough in parchment paper and transfer to freezer for 15-20 minutes until hard.
Using bread knife, slice dough into ¼-inch rounds. Transfer to sheet trays and bake 10-15 minutes or until lightly golden. Cool and serve.

recipes.name: RUGELACH
recipes.description: (FALL/WINTER)
instructions: In food processor, combine cream cheese and butter. Process until smooth and creamy. Add maple crystals and vanilla; process until incorporated, scraping sides of bowl as necessary.
In small bowl, whisk together flour and salt. Add to food processor. Pulse until dough starts to clump together and form ball.
Remove dough from food processor. Separate dough equally in two and wrap each piece in plastic and flatten to disc shape. Refrigerate for at least one and one half hours until firm.
In medium bowl, combine currants, walnuts, maple crystals, and cinnamon. Set aside. Place preserves into separate small bowl. Set aside.
Pre-heat oven to 350°F, line 2 half sheet pans with parchment paper.

Work with one dough at a time, leaving other in refrigerator. Liberally dust dough with flour. Roll between 2 pieces of plastic wrap to 9-inch circle. Thickness should be 1/8 inch. Use inverted nine-inch cake pan to trim edges.
Using offset spatula, spread dough with half of preserves. Sprinkle with 1/2 of filling. Divide circle into 16 even “slices” (using bench knife, pizza cutter, or sharp knife).
Starting at wide end of triangle, roll each slice tightly as possible. Transfer to sheet tray and refrigerate 15-20 minutes more. Repeat steps 7-10 with remaining dough.
Before baking, brush each cookie with egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes or until lightly golden.

recipes.name: Salted Almond and Thyme Brittle
instructions: Line 2 half-sheet pans with Silpat and set aside. Have 2 more Silpats ready for use.
In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine brown rice syrup, water, coconut oil, agave, and salt. Set pot over medium flame, stirring occasionally, until mixture comes to boil. Reduce heat to simmer.
Once mixture reaches 260°F as measured on candy thermometer, add thyme. Do not stir mixture again but swirl pot occasionally and keep cooking until candy thermometer reads 280°F.
Stir in nuts and mix well. Remove mixture from heat and thoroughly stir in baking soda.

Quickly divide brittle mixture between 2 half-sheet pans, using lightly oiled spatula. Spread brittle into thin even layer. Place second large Silpat on top of brittle and roll more thinly with rolling pin.
Let brittle cool completely, about 30 minutes. If making brittle on hot, humid day in kitchen without air conditioning, then you may have to cool brittle in refrigerator.
When cooled, turn brittle upside down from Silpat to parchment paper. Break brittle in 1/4-inch sized pieces.

recipes.name: Salted Pecan and Rosemary Brittle
instructions: Line 2 half-sheet pans with Silpats and set aside. Have 2 more Silpats ready for use.
In 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine brown rice syrup, water, coconut oil, agave, and salt. Set pot over medium flame, stirring occasionally, until mixture comes to boil. Reduce heat to simmer.
Once mixture reaches 260°F as measured on candy thermometer, add rosemary. Do not stir mixture again but swirl pot occasionally and keep cooking until candy thermometer reads 280°F.
Stir in nuts and mix well. Remove mixture from heat and thoroughly stir in baking soda.

Quickly divide brittle mixture between 2 half-sheet pans, using lightly oiled spatula. Spread brittle into thin even layer. Place second large Silpat on top of brittle and roll more thinly with rolling pin.
Let brittle cool completely, about 30 minutes. If making brittle on hot, humid day in kitchen without air conditioning, then you may have to cool brittle in refrigerator.
When cooled, turn brittle upside down from Silpat onto parchment paper. Break brittle in 1/4-inch sized pieces.

recipes.name: SESAME ANISE BISCOTTI
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line half-sheet tray with parchment paper.
In food processor, grind almonds to fine meal. In spice grinder, grind sesame seeds and anise seeds into fine powder. Add sesame seeds, anise, and baking powder to food processor and process.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil, syrup, extracts, and sea salt.

Add wet ingredients to dry in food processor. Pulse until dough comes together. Separate dough into 2 equal parts. Pour sesame seeds on plate. Gently press and roll logs in sesame seeds to cover all sides.
On cutting board, shape both doughs into perfectly matching rectangles (approximately 3 inches wide by 6 inches long) using 2 dough scrapers. Freeze dough before slicing.
Using sharp chef’s knife, slice each log into ¼ inch thick slices.
Transfer slices on sheet tray to oven and cook approximately 7 minutes each side or until thoroughly golden and crisp.

recipes.name: SESAME PRESSED CRUST

ingredients.name: chilled juice or water to bind

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil 9-inch pie or tart pan.
Process together whole wheat pastry flour, oatmeal, sesame seeds and salt until mixture is uniformly flour-like.
Whisk together oil and syrup.
Add oil-syrup mixture to processor and mix until thoroughly combined. Add juice or water if more liquid is needed.
With wet fingertips, press mixture into oiled pie plate.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden.

recipes.name: SHEPHERD’S PIE

ingredients.name: arrowroot dissolved in 3 teaspoons cold water

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Partially 'blind bake' pie shell (about 10 minutes) and set aside.
In 10-inch sauté pan, heat olive oil. Add onion, garlic, carrots, parsnips, and fresh thyme. Sauté until slightly tender. Add couple tablespoons water to deglaze pan.
Mix together sesame oil, tamari, and mustard; stir into vegetable mixture in sauté pan. Continue to cook another 10 minutes, and transfer mixture to bowl.
In separate 10-inch sauté pan, heat olive oil, add seitan and cook until seitan is slightly browned. Add wine and continue cooking until wine is absorbed. Add seitan to bowl with cooked vegetables.

Thicken reduced stock by adding arrowroot slurry and simmering until mixture thickens. Add this mixture to bowl containing vegetables and seitan. Season mixture with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside to cool.
In 1-gallon pot, boil potatoes until tender. Drain. Process potatoes through ricer or food mill. Season with soy milk, butter or olive oil, salt and pepper. Cover and set aside.
Fill partially baked pie shell with vegetable/seitan mixture. Using pastry bag fitted with tip, pipe potato mixture onto top of pie.
Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until vegetables are fork tender and crust is fully baked. Remove from oven and garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.name: SHORTBREAD COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 300° F and line half sheet tray with parchment paper.
Cream butter, sugar, vanilla and salt in stand mixer.
Gradually sift in flour until well mixed.

Firmly press dough into flattened 6-inch oval in center of sheet tray. Cut dough into 16 equal-sized slices and pierce each slice with fork in decorative design (be sure to pierce through to pan to allow excess steam to escape).
Bake about 45-50 minutes or until entire dough is golden brown and firm to touch.
Remove from oven and cool on wire rack. Retrace cuts in dough to loosen cookies but allow to remain on sheet tray to fully cool (do not move cookies as they are very fragile at this stage).

recipes.name: Skewered Fruit with Chocolate Fondue
instructions: Skewer fruit as follows: banana-kiwi-pineapple-strawberry-orange-strawberry-pineapple-kiwi-banana. Serve with Chocolate Fondue (recipe below).

recipes.name: Sour Cream Coffee Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease a deep 9-inch Bundt mold with butter and dust with flour. Set aside.
In bowl, stir together the filling mixture until well mixed and set aside.
In stand mixer, cream butter and maple crystals. Add eggs one at a time, and beat until well incorporated. Add sour cream and mix until batter is smooth. Add vanilla.
Sift together flour, salt, and baking soda. Add dry ingredients to wet in stand mixer, and mix until batter is smooth.
Pour batter in prepared cake pan. Sprinkle crumble mixture over batter. Pour remainder of batter atop filling.
Bake cake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick or skewer inserted in cake comes out smooth.
Let cake sit in pan for approximately 15 minutes before unmolding onto cooling rack. Cook cake completely before slicing.

recipes.name: SPICE LOAF RING
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour 9 or 10-inch non-stick Bundt pan.
In food processor, combine butter and maple crystals. Process 2-3 minutes. Add eggs one at a time. Add almond extract. Continue to blend 2-3 minutes longer. Transfer to medium bowl.
In separate medium bowl, sift together flours, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt.
Fold flour mixture into butter egg mixture (batter will be slightly thick).
Pour batter into Bundt pan (should be about 2/3 full).
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Cool in pan about 10 minutes. Run knife around edge to loosen cake from pan. Cool completely on rack.

recipes.name: Spiced Carrot Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in large bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well. Add additional ingredients and mix to combine.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 45-50 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pans.
Cool in pans on wire rack for about 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and allow to completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: Sticky Buns
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Whisk together syrup ingredients, combine raisin-walnut filling; set both aside.
In large bowl, combine warm water, maple syrup, and yeast. Proof for 5-10 minutes, or until yeast is activated (foamy). Add melted coconut oil.
In separate large bowl, whisk together flours and salt.
Add enough flour mixture to yeast mixture to create dough that pulls away from sides.
Knead dough about 10 minutes to form soft, smooth dough, using flour as necessary.
Transfer dough to clean, large bowl. Cover with plastic wrap, and rise until doubled in size (about 30 minutes to 1 hour).
Fold/turn dough. Rise one more time.

Cut dough in half and roll each half to 1/4-inch thick rectangle. Spread 1/3 syrup mixture over dough. Sprinkle 1/2 raisins and walnuts on top. Roll dough into cylinder. Repeat process with second dough.
Cut rolled dough into 2-inch rounds and arrange nestled in two oiled 9-inch cake pans lined with parchment.
Rise dough until doubled in size, approximately 15-20 minutes.
Bake for 25 minutes. Brush remaining 1/3 syrup mixture on top, rotate pans, and bake for 10-15 minutes more or until firm to touch and golden. Cool and unmold.

recipes.name: STRAWBERRY SORBET
recipes.description: (SPRING/SUMMER)
instructions: In blender, puree strawberries, maple syrup, agave syrup, and balsamic vinegar until smooth. Transfer mixture to medium bowl and whisk in salt, pepper, and basil.

Transfer mixture to ice cream machine and freeze according to directions. Remove sorbet from canister and transfer to 9-pan. Freeze forty minutes to one hour or until sorbet firms to scoop-able consistency.

recipes.name: SWEET CRANBERRY TART

ingredients.name: kuzu dissolved in 1/3 cup orange juice

instructions: In 1-gallon pot, mix cranberries, maple syrup, and currants. Bring mixture to boil, reduce to simmer, and cook until all cranberries have popped.
In 2 1/2 quart pot, bring apple juice and agar to boil. Reduce heat and cook until agar is dissolved. Stir into cranberry mixture.
Mix together kuzu/orange juice slurry and orange zest. Stir kuzu slurry into cranberry mixture and cook until mixture is clear. Remove from heat and add walnuts. Chill to cool.
Spoon filling into baked tart shell and chill to set.

recipes.name: SWEET POTATO PECAN PIE
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Roll out pie dough and line pie plate. After dough has rested in refrigerator for 15 minutes, trim and form edges, cover and chill for another 30 minutes.
In bowl of food processor, combine yams, maple crystals, kuzu and soymilk, oil, spices, and extracts. Process until well blended, scraping sides of bowl often.

In 2 1/2 quart pot, over medium heat, bring agar and water to boil. Reduce heat, cover, and cook until agar is dissolved. Add agar mixture to yam mixture in food processor and blend for 1-2 minutes. Set aside.
Combine maple syrup and rice syrup and set aside.
Pour filling into pie shell. Arrange pecans on top of filling and drizzle syrup mixture over top of pie.
Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake for 40 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean and crust is firm. Remove foil from edges 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool pie to set filling before serving (about 30 minutes).

recipes.name: SWISS BURNT PECAN TART

ingredients.name: barley malt syrup dissolved in 2 teaspoons water

instructions: Preheat oven to 275°F.
Roast pecans for about 40 minutes. Remove from pan and allow to completely cool.
Raise oven temperature to 350°F.
Roll out half the dough and transfer to tart pan. Chill 15 minutes. Trim edges, allowing 1-inch overhang. Chill rolled dough for another 15 minutes.
Roll out other half of dough and transfer to sheet pan. Cover and chill until ready to use.
In bowl of food processor, grind pecans to coarse flour. Add syrups, arrowroot, and vanilla. Mix to combine.
Pour filling into tart shell. Place top dough over filling, trim and seal edges. Cut a few steam vents.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until crust is firm. Brush top with glaze 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool and set before serving (about 30 minutes).

recipes.name: Tapioca Pudding
instructions: In 1-gallon pot, combine soaked and drained tapioca, almond milk, salt, rice syrup, and maple syrup. Whisk together. Bring mixture to simmer over burner with flame tamer, stirring constantly to keep tapioca from sticking to bottom of pot.
Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture starts to thicken, and tapioca just becomes translucent, about 10-15 minutes. Do not overcook or mixture will become glue-like.
Stir in vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Remove from heat. Let mixture cool down, and chill further in refrigerator.

recipes.name: TOASTED WALNUT CRUST (FOR LIGHT LEMON TART)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil and parchment 8 or 9-inch tart pan. Alternatively, use 5-6 four-inch, non-stick paper tart pans.
Combine nuts, flour, maple crystals, and salt in food processor. Grind to fine meal.
Add syrup and oil to processor. Pulse to form dough.
Place dough in middle of tart pan. Using your fingertips, press dough out so that bottom and sides are evenly covered. Trim crust and discard any excess. Blot excess oil from crust with paper towel.
Transfer tart pan(s) to refrigerator for 10-15 minutes to chill.
Transfer tart pan(s) to sheet tray and bake about 20 minutes. Cool completely before filling.

recipes.name: TRI-COLOR FRUIT TERRINE

ingredients.name: pitted frozen cherries or 1 bag frozen cherries

instructions: Lightly brush terrine mold with oil and line with parchment paper, making sure inside of pan is covered entirely.

For first layer of terrine, process pineapple and one banana (broken into pieces) through Champion juicer using blank screen. Spoon pineapple-banana mixture into terrine mold and spread with offset spatula until surface is flat and even. Transfer terrine to freezer while preparing next layer.

For second layer, process frozen strawberries and remaining banana (broken into pieces) through Champion juicer using blank screen. Adjust flavor of blended fruit with lemon juice and maple syrup to taste, stirring well to combine. Spoon and smooth strawberry-banana mixture atop pineapple-banana mixture. Transfer terrine to freezer while preparing next layer.

For final layer, repeat previous step with frozen cherries. Add maple syrup to cherry puree and spoon atop strawberry-banana mixture. Cover terrine with plastic wrap, and freeze entire terrine until firm to touch (1 1/2 to 2 hours).
To serve, turn terrine out of mold and remove parchment. Allow terrine to thaw slightly (about 2 minutes) before slicing.

recipes.name: Truffled Portobello Mousse
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Combine navy beans and bay leaf in pressure cooker. Add water to cover by 2 inches. Cover cooker and bring beans to pressure. Reduce heat and cook for 20 minutes. Release pressure by placing pressure cooker under cold water and drain beans, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
Toss 2 tablespoons of olive oil with sliced mushrooms and 1/2 teaspoon sea salt. Spread mushrooms on parchment-lined sheet tray and roast 15 minutes, or until golden.
In large sauté pan, heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Add onions and remaining 1/2 teaspoon of salt and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or until onions are golden. Deglaze pan with sherry.

Combine agar flakes and reserved cup of bean cooking liquid in 2-quart saucepan. Bring mixture to a simmer, cook for 8 to 10 minutes (with lid ajar) or until the agar is completely dissolved, stirring occasionally.
Combine navy beans, Portobello mushrooms, onions, dissolved agar mixture and truffle salt in Vitamix. Using tamper, blend mixture for 3 to 5 minutes, or until completely smooth.
Pour mixture into silicone molds and refrigerate for 30 to 60 minutes to set.
Coat sides of unmolded mousse with thyme leaves before serving.
Serve chilled atop sliced baguette with fig-thyme preserves (see below for recipe).

recipes.name: Vanilla Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection oven). Oil and flour one 8-inch cake pan. Line bottom of pan with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 30-40 minutes until cake is springy to touch and pulls away from sides of pan.
Cool in pan on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pan and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: Vegan and Gluten-Free Chocolate Brownies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (convection oven to 300°F). Oil and flour 9-inch square pan and line with parchment.
In bowl, whisk together almond flour, sorghum flour, tapioca flour, cocoa powder, salt, and baking powder. Process to combine. Transfer dry ingredients to bowl.

In separate bowl set over simmering water, melt 1 cup of chocolate and coconut oil. Remove from heat and whisk chocolate and coconut oil together. Stir in kuzu-water mixture, coconut sugar, coconut milk, and vanilla. Whisk wet ingredients to emulsify.
Pour wet mixture into dry and stir well. The batter should be stiff. Fold in walnuts and remaining 1/4 cup chocolate.
Transfer batter to pan, place parchment atop brownie. Smooth surface with hands until even.
Bake 30 minutes. Cool in pan for about 1 hour (otherwise brownie will crack when cut). Cut edges of brownie away from sides of pan before removing from pan.

recipes.name: VEGAN BAKLAVA
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
For phyllo: In bowl, mix nuts and cinnamon. Set aside.
In half-sheet pan lined with parchment paper, individually oil and layer 6-7 sheets of phyllo. Edges of phyllo sheets will overhang bottom of sheet pan slightly, but they will be trimmed later.

Spread portion of nut mixture (approximately 1/3-1/2 cups) over top of phyllo, enough to cover surface. Add another sheet of brushed phyllo and cover with more nuts; repeat this process until all nuts are gone.
Top baklava with 6 more layers of oil-brushed phyllo. Trim excess phyllo from sides of pan, so phyllo fits pan exactly.
Cut baklava into eighths lengthwise. Then make diagonal crosswise cuts, at 2-inch intervals.
Bake baklava 30 minutes at 300°F in standard oven (fan in convection oven causes phyllo to blow away). Bake additional 30 minutes at 350°F, until golden brown.
For syrup: While baklava bakes, bring all syrup ingredients to simmer in 2-quart saucepan. Cook syrup uncovered until reduced to 2 cups.
Remove baklava from oven. Pour hot syrup over warm phyllo and let sit at least 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Vegan Cashew Cream
instructions: Combine cashews, vanilla, brown rice vinegar, salt, and maple syrup in Vitamix with wand attachment. Start blending on low speed, and slowly raise speed while stirring with wand.
When mixture is starting to smooth, add water, and continue processing. When mixture is almost smooth, turn Vitamix up to highest setting. Finished cream should be thick and pipe-able.

recipes.name: Vegan Pastry Crust
instructions: In medium bowl, sift together dry ingredients. Use whisk to fully combine ingredients.
Add oil to bowl. Using pastry cutter, blend oil into flour. Dough should have coarse, sand-like consistency.
Add vanilla and maple syrup to dough with wooden spoon. Mix to combine.
Slowly add water to dough one tablespoon at a time. Dough should just hold together and be moist (but not wet).
Place dough in plastic wrap, twisting so it holds together. Flatten to disc shape and refrigerate 10-15 minutes.
Remove dough from refrigerator; rest it until workable and can be rolled without cracking.

Lightly dust a sheet of parchment with all-purpose flour. Lay dough atop parchment and lightly dust surface of dough. Place second piece of parchment paper on top of dough, and roll out, flipping halfway. Remove second piece of parchment and continue rolling until dough is 1/8 inch thick.

Invert 9-inch pie plate over center of rolled out dough. Using sharp knife, cut a circle using cake pan as a guide. If dough is too soft, refrigerate briefly until it is firm enough to work with but not so firm that is cracks when assembling the galette.

recipes.name: WALNUT TEA COOKIES
instructions: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Cream butter and maple crystals in stand mixer until fluffy and well combined, about 5 minutes. Add vanilla and salt until mixed.

In separate smaller bowl, whisk together flours. Slowly sift flours into butter mixture in stand mixer, until all flour is incorporated. Add in walnuts. Divide dough in 2 and wrap each in plastic. Refrigerate 10-15 minutes.
Remove 1 dough from refrigerator. Roll between parchment paper to 1/4" thickness. Freeze dough until hard. Cut shapes from dough using cookie cutters. Repeat process with second dough.
Bake about 6 minutes. Rotate baking pans and continue to bake about 5-6 more minutes or until lightly golden. Remove cookies from pans to racks to cool.

recipes.name: WATERMELON GRANITA
recipes.description: (SPRING/SUMMER)
instructions: Blend watermelon in Vitamix and strain out excess pulp with nut bag or chinois lined with 2 layers of moistened cheesecloth.
Transfer watermelon juice to medium bowl and add lime juice, agave, and salt.
Pour mixture into half hotel pan (mixture should be about 1/4 inch up side of pan) and transfer to freezer for about 1 hour.
Remove pan from freezer and use fork to scrape any ice crystals that have formed on side or bottom of pan. Return to freezer and repeat scraping every 30 minutes for 3-4 hours.
Once mixture is thoroughly frozen, scrape once more with fork, returning granita to “dry” in freezer for another half hour before serving.
Garnish granita with mint sprigs and serve.

recipes.name: Whipped Cream
instructions: Combine all ingredients in stand mixer fitted with chilled bowl and whip until stiff peaks form.

recipes.name: Zesty Lemon Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pans.
Cool in pans on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

recipes.name: ADZUKI BEAN STEW
instructions: In 1-gallon pot on medium-low flame, heat oil. Add onion, salt, and garlic. Sweat until onions become translucent. Add aduki beans, kombu, and stock. Cover and bring to boil over high heat, reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, for 30 minutes or until beans are almost tender.
Add butternut squash, cover, and continue simmering 20 minutes or until beans, onions, and squash are tender.
Remove kombu. Add ginger juice and tamari. Season to taste.
Garnish with scallions and serve.

recipes.name: AIRLINE CHICKEN BREASTS WITH COMPOUND BUTTER

ingredients.name: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Combine chicken breasts in medium bowl with water and salt to brine. Refrigerate one hour. Remove breasts from water and dry well.
Combine butter, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, and basil in food processor. Process until ingredients are well incorporated and butter is smooth.
Remove compound butter mixture from processor and divide into 4 equal portions. Set aside.
Preheat convection oven to 400°F.
Gently separate skin from breast, taking care not to tear it. Spread compound butter evenly between skin and breast. Season skin with salt and pepper.
Heat ghee in 12-inch sauté pan. Place breasts skin side down in pan. Sear over medium-high heat to caramelize skin.
Transfer pan to oven and roast breasts for 15-20 minutes or until juices run clear. Do not turn chicken over while cooking. Serve skin side up.

recipes.name: Baked Tofu
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F.
Slice each slab of tofu into 16 cubes.
In a small baking vessel, combine tofu with cumin, paprika, garlic powder, apple juice, tamari, and oil.
Transfer to oven and bake 15 - 20 minutes. Remove from oven and serve with Romesco Sauce.

recipes.name: Barbecue Tofu
instructions: Cut tofu in half horizontally (about 3/4” thick). Press fifteen minutes between paper towels.
Slice tofu into finger-sized pieces (about 1 inch wide).
Heat grill, brush with canola or coconut oil. Place tofu on griddle. Grill on each side about 2-3 minutes or until grill marks appear.
In large sauté pan, combine all marinade ingredients. Transfer tofu to marinade and simmer gently 25-30 minutes or place sauté pan in 350° oven for 20 minutes.
Remove tofu from pan. Reduce sauce to desired consistency.

recipes.name: BASIC BROILED CHICKEN
instructions: Preheat broiler 20 minutes prior to using. Adjust rack to lowest setting.
Rub both skin side and inside of chicken with olive oil, salt, and fresh ground black pepper.
Heat 10-inch sauté pan over medium flame and place chicken, skin side down, in pan. Do not add any extra oil to pan. Transfer chicken to broiler.

Broil chicken skin side down for 15 minutes. Carefully flip chicken skin side up, and continue to broil for another 20 minutes. Depending on size of chicken, full cooking may need to be completed in preheated convection oven at 400°F for another 10-15 minutes.

recipes.name: BASIC CHICKEN STOCK
instructions: Combine bones, onion, carrot, celery, sachet, and water in large stock pot.
Cover pot and bring to boil. Remove cover and skim any foam off top.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 3-4 hours.
Strain stock immediately, first through china cap, then chinois.
Cool stock in ice bath and refrigerate.

recipes.name: BASIC SEITAN RECIPE

ingredients.name: extra white bread flour for kneading

instructions: In 1-gallon pot, combine water, shoyu, ginger, garlic, bay leaf, and kombu. Bring stock to boil, reduce to simmer, and cover.
Combine flours in large mixing bowl, stirring well. Pour in water gradually, stirring to form dough that comes together in a ball. Add only enough water until dough is kneadable consistency.
Knead dough well to thoroughly and evenly develop gluten, about 15 minutes. Add extra flour if dough gets too sticky.
Cover dough with cold water in bowl and keep submerged for at least 30 minutes. Dough can be stored in refrigerator overnight and rinsed next day. As dough rests, gluten continues to develop.
Transfer dough from bowl to colander and place in sink. Under warm running water, carefully knead dough, rinsing out starch and bran. Water will become milky as starch comes out.

At a certain point, it will seem as though dough is falling apart. After several minutes of rinsing and kneading, however, gluten will start to tighten again. Continue to knead dough until it has firm, tight, and rubbery texture.
Pull pieces of gluten into small billiard-size balls. Drop gluten into stock, one piece at a time, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Simmer seitan for 1 ½ to 2 hours, depending on size of pieces.
For improved flavor and firmer texture, cool seitan to room temperature in broth. Store in refrigerator, submerged in broth, or freeze.
Note: The amount of shoyu added to broth depends on how and if stock will be used in recipes. If planning to reduce broth as part of a sauce, do not make it too salty.

recipes.name: Basic Tempeh
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine shoyu, ginger, kombu, sea salt, and tempeh. Pour in enough water to cover tempeh (about 3 cups). Cover pan and bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer about 20-25 minutes.
Drain tempeh and set aside. Reserve cooking liquid for use in Tempeh Scaloppini.

recipes.name: BEET PASTA
instructions: Place beet in medium saucepan and cover with water. Boil until tender, about 1 hour. Drain and cool beet.
Slip skin off beet, puree, put beet through food mill or potato ricer. (Do not put into food processor or it will be too wet.)
Transfer beet puree to fine sieve over bowl or sink, pressing down occasionally with back of large spoon, until most of water has drained off.
Reserve 1 tablespoon of puree for pasta; discard remaining puree or save for another use.
Follow either method below.
Method - Food Processor:

Pulse flour in food processor to evenly distribute and aerate. Add eggs and beet puree, process until dough forms rough ball, about 30 seconds. If dough resembles small pebbles, add water, 1/2 teaspoon at a time; if dough sticks to sides of bowl, add flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, and process until dough forms rough ball.
Turn dough onto work surface; knead until dough is smooth, 1 to 2 minutes. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside for at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours to relax.
Method - By Hand:
Sift flour onto work surface (or bowl) in mound and make hollow in middle. Break eggs into hollow and add beet puree. With fork, start to mix in flour from edge.

Gradually incorporate most of flour until viscous paste begins to form. Put fork to one side and, using both hands, heap remaining flour from outside over paste in middle. Work flour into paste. If paste does not absorb all flour, and if ingredients cannot be easily worked, add a little water.

Work in water with both thumbs, then press dough into ball and work in rest of flour. Knead dough by pushing out dough with heels of hands, then form it into ball again. Repeat this kneading action until dough has firm but slightly elastic consistency and no longer changes shape when you remove your hands. Cover with plastic wrap and rest minimum of fifteen minutes.

recipes.name: BLACK PEPPER PASTA
instructions: Method - Food Processor:

Pulse flour and black pepper in food processor to evenly distribute and aerate. Add eggs, process until dough forms rough ball, about 30 seconds. If dough resembles small pebbles, add water, 1/2 teaspoon at a time; if dough sticks to sides of bowl, add flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, and process until dough forms rough ball.
Turn dough onto work surface; knead until dough is smooth, 1 to 2 minutes. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside for at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours to relax.
Method - By Hand:
Sift flour and pepper onto work surface (or bowl) in mound and make hollow in middle. Break eggs into hollow. With fork, start to mix in flour from edge.

Gradually incorporate most of flour until viscous paste begins to form. Put fork to one side and, using both hands, heap remaining flour from outside over paste in middle. Work flour into paste. If paste does not absorb all flour, and if ingredients cannot be easily worked, add a little water.

Work in water with both thumbs, then press dough into ball and work in rest of flour. Knead dough by pushing out dough with heels of hands, then form it into ball again. Repeat this kneading action until dough has firm but slightly elastic consistency and no longer changes shape when you remove your hands. Cover with plastic wrap and rest minimum of fifteen minutes.

recipes.name: Black Quinoa with Capers and Rapini (for Broiled Arctic Char)
instructions: Combine quinoa with vegetable stock and salt in small saucepan. Bring to boil, reduce to simmer, and cook covered approximately 15 to 20 minutes or until stock is absorbed. Remove from heat, uncover pot and allow quinoa to rest 10 minutes.
In separate pot, bring 2 quarts of salted water to boil. Prepare ice bath. Blanch rapini for 3 minutes, shock in ice water, and drain. Squeeze out excess liquid.
Roughly chop rapini and set aside.
Heat oil in small sauté pan over low flame, add garlic, cooking briefly until just golden. Do not let garlic brown.
Transfer garlic and one tablespoon oil from pan to food processor. Add rapini. Pulse mixture until very finely chopped. Add basil and pulse again.
Transfer rapini mixture to bowl and thoroughly mix with quinoa, capers, black pepper, and lemon zest.
Divide quinoa-rapini mixture among four plates, placing Arctic Char filet atop each portion.

recipes.name: Blackened Shrimp
instructions: In shallow pan or plate, distribute Blackening Spice Mix evenly.
Skewer shrimp, 3 to skewer.
Roll skewered shrimp in spice mix. Heat griddle grill.
Grill shrimp about 1 1/2-2 minutes on each side until shrimp is opaque.

recipes.name: BOILED NOODLES – SHOCK METHOD
instructions: Bring water to boil over medium heat. Add salt if needed.
Add noodles and stir to separate them.
Cover pot. Bring to rolling boil. Add 1/2 cup cold water and stir noodles.

Bring to rolling boil again. Add 1/2 cup cold water and stir noodles. Bring to rolling boil a third time. Add 1/2 cup cold water and stir noodles. Bring to rolling boil again. Remove from heat and let stand 2 to 3 minutes. Noodles are done when they are the same color inside and out.
Drain and rinse in cold water until noodles are cooled.

Note: This method of shocking noodles involves bringing noodles to rolling boil (noodles almost foam out of the pan) and adding cold water three times. The cold water temporarily halts cooking of outside of noodles so inside of noodles can become soft (without overcooking outside). Noodles cooked by shocking will be cooked uniformly throughout.

recipes.name: BRAISED CHICKEN WITH VEGETABLES AND TARRAGON
instructions: Heat oven to 325°F.
Toss chicken legs in bowl with flour, salt, and pepper to thoroughly coat.
Heat oil in 12-inch sauté pan on medium-high flame.
When oil is hot, lower heat and sear chicken on both sides, being careful not to burn it.
Add carrots, celery, onion, and flour; sauté for 1 minute. Add potatoes, salt, pepper, and sachet. Stir in white wine to deglaze. Add stock, cover pot, and bring braise to boil.
Transfer pan to oven and cook for 40-45 minutes or until chicken is thoroughly cooked and vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Garnish with tarragon. Season to taste and serve.

recipes.name: Broiled Arctic Char Over Black Quinoa, Rapini, and Capers

ingredients.name: black quinoa with capers and rapini

instructions: Heat salamander and set rack on highest setting.
Combine salt and pepper, and sprinkle over char.
Lightly coat sizzle platter with oil and arrange fish on top.
Sprinkle remaining oil and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice atop each portion of fish.
Broil char under salamander for approximately 3 minutes.
Serve over Black Quinoa (recipe below).

recipes.name: Brown Basmati Rice Variation #1
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In small baking dish, dry roast rice in oven until dry. Stir oil into rice and bake few minutes more, stirring occasionally.
Add water and spices to rice; cover baking dish tightly with tin foil.
Cook covered, about 50 to 60 minutes, or until all water is absorbed.

recipes.name: Brown Basmati Rice Variation #3
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In small baking dish, dry roast rice in oven until dry. Stir oil into rice and bake few minutes more, stirring occasionally.
Add water, salt, galangal, and lemongrass to rice; cover tightly with tin foil.
Cook covered, about 50 to 60 minutes, or until all water is absorbed.

recipes.name: BROWN VEGETABLE STOCK
instructions: Preheat oven to 400-425°F.
In large stockpot, combine white beans, lentils, and ten quarts water. Bring to boil, covered, skimming foam as needed. Reduce heat to simmer and continue to cook partially covered.

Mix carrots, onions, shallots, celery, and parsnips with oil. Roast on large oiled baking sheet, stirring occasionally, until browned and aromatic. Add tomatoes and garlic to vegetables in oven near end of roasting time. Add roasted vegetables to bean stockpot.
Deglaze baking sheet with white wine. Add deglaze liquid, walnuts, bouquet garni, and shoyu to bean stockpot. Simmer, partially covered, for 60-90 minutes. Strain immediately.

recipes.name: BUCKWHEAT PASTA
instructions: Pulse flours in food processor to evenly distribute and aerate. Add eggs, process until dough forms rough ball, about 30 seconds. If dough resembles small pebbles, add water, 1/2 teaspoon at a time; if dough sticks to sides of bowl, add flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, and process until dough forms rough ball.
Turn dough onto work surface; knead until dough is smooth, 1 to 2 minutes. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside for at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours to relax.
Sift flours onto work surface (or bowl) in mound and make hollow in middle. Break eggs into hollow. With fork, start to mix in flour from edge.

Gradually incorporate most of flour until viscous paste begins to form. Put fork to one side and, using both hands, heap remaining flour from outside over paste in middle. Work flour into paste. If paste does not absorb all flour, and if ingredients cannot be easily worked, add a little water.

Work in water with both thumbs, then press dough into ball and work in rest of flour. Knead dough by pushing out dough with heels of hands, then form it into ball again. Repeat this kneading action until dough has firm but slightly elastic consistency and no longer changes shape when you remove your hands. Cover with plastic wrap and rest minimum of fifteen minutes.

recipes.name: Bulgur
instructions: Dry roast bulgur in small sauté pan.
Bring water and salt to boil in small saucepot, add bulgur, cover and bring back to a rolling boil for 1 minute.
Remove pot from heat. Let steam, covered, 45 minutes.

recipes.name: BULGUR RAISIN BREAD
instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F. Prepare two 5 x 9 loaf pans with parchment. In medium bowl, combine water, maple crystals, and yeast. Proof for 10 minutes or until mixture is foamy.

Add salt, oil, cinnamon, allspice, vanilla, bulgur wheat, raisins, white high-gluten flour, and all-purpose flour. Then add just enough whole wheat pastry flour to create dough that pulls away from sides of bowl.
Knead dough adding remaining pastry flour as needed for about 10-15 minutes or until smooth dough has been created.
Transfer dough to large, clean, lightly oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Proof in warm place for 45-60 minutes or until dough has doubled in size.
While dough is proofing, prepare bread pans or sheet pans with parchment.
Fold/turn dough. Rise again.

Divide dough into two equally sized balls. Roll each dough to a long rectangle, about 1/2-inch thick. Spread maple crystals and cinnamon over surface of dough. Roll dough lengthwise, jelly-roll style and transfer to loaf pans, seam side down.
Cover dough with wet towels and set aside in warm place. Rise until dough has doubled in size.
Bake approximately 30 minutes or until dough is golden and firm to touch. Internal dough temperature should be approximately 190°-205° F.
Cool bread on racks (out of pan) before serving.

recipes.name: CASSOULET

ingredients.name: whole wheat bread crumbs mixed with 3 tablespoons olive oil

instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Combine beans in pot with salt, kombu, Brown Stock, and sachet. Cover and cook at simmer until beans are soft (approximately 45 minutes).
Toss carrots and parsnips in bowl with 3 tablespoons olive oil, transfer to parchment-lined sheet tray, and roast until browned (about 20 to 25 minutes). Sprinkle with salt and set aside.

In 10-inch sauté pan, caramelize onions with 2 tablespoons of oil. When softened and browned, add garlic and cook few minutes more. Add tomatoes and remaining oil. Sauté until tomatoes are soft. Set aside.

When beans are tender, add tomatoes and onions to pot. Simmer 5 minutes more. Strain bean mixture, reserving bean liquid. Reduce liquid over heat until nappé consistency is achieved (should lightly coat back of spoon). Add reduction back into bean/tomato mixture and season with salt and pepper.
In small bowl, combine parsley, thyme, and marjoram with breadcrumbs and olive oil.
In 2-quart casserole dish, layer alternately beans and roasted vegetables. Top with breadcrumb mixture. Bake uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes until browned.

recipes.name: CHICKEN BREASTS IN MUSHROOM SAUCE
instructions: In shallow bowl, dredge chicken in flour. Shake off excess flour.
In 10-inch sauté pan, heat 3 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken in oil until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove chicken from pan, season immediately with salt and pepper, cover to keep warm, and let rest for 10 minutes.

Add remaining oil to pan and heat over medium-high flame. Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes. Add shallots and garlic and continue cooking until mushrooms turn golden brown (2 to 3 minutes), stirring often to prevent garlic and shallots from burning.
Pour wine into pan and cook over high heat until almost evaporated, scraping browned bits from bottom of pan. Add stock and cook until reduced by half.
Remove pan from heat and whisk in butter. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Slice chicken thinly on bias and arrange by fanning slices.

recipes.name: CHICKEN KOTLETKY (CHICKEN BURGERS)
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F.
Toss bread crumbs and milk in medium-size bowl until bread has soaked up all milk. Combine bread crumb mixture with ground chicken, onions, dill weed, salt, and pepper.
Using 1/4 cup measure, portion chicken burgers.
Heat oil in 12-inch sauté pan over medium-high flame, and lightly brown patties on both sides.
Transfer burgers from sauté pan to half sheet tray lined with parchment.
Transfer burgers to oven and bake for 15 minutes.
Garnish with sour cream and fresh dill sprigs.

recipes.name: CHICKEN POT PIE FILLING WITH TOASTED BREADCRUMBS
instructions: Heat convection oven to 400°F.

Combine thighs and oil in bowl. Coat thighs with 1/4 cup olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer chicken to parchment-lined half sheet pan, skin side up, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until cooked through but still moist. After chicken has cooled enough to handle, remove and discard skin and bones. Cut chicken into large dice and set aside.

In 1-gallon pot, melt butter over medium flame. Add onion and sweat until translucent (about 10 minutes). Stir in flour and continue to cook over low heat about 7-8 minutes, stirring constantly. Add chicken stock and simmer over low heat for another 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Bring 1 gallon water to boil and add 1 tablespoon salt. Prepare ice bath. Blanch carrots and celery for 5 minutes in boiling, salted water. Shock in ice water, drain, and set aside.
Add chicken, carrots, celery, peas, and fresh thyme to pot with chicken stock and continue to cook over low heat for an additional 5 minutes. Check seasoning and adjust if necessary.

Heat 10-inch sauté pan over low heat. Add Panko and remaining 2 tablespoons of oil. Carefully sauté Panko until golden brown. Add parsley and season lightly with salt and pepper, continuing to toast 2 minutes more.
Divide pot pie mixture equally between 8 bowls and top with breadcrumb mixture.

recipes.name: CHICKEN UNDER A BRICK
instructions: Heat convection oven to 400°F.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in 10-inch sauté pan over high flame. When oil is hot but not yet smoking, add chicken, skin side down. Place foil covered brick on top of chicken. Sear for 5 minutes.
Transfer pan to oven and cook for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and remove brick.
Turn chicken skin side up, and carefully pour off excess fat.
Transfer pan back to oven for additional 5-10 minutes, with fan turned to high.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: CHICKPEA CRÊPES
recipes.description: Vegan
instructions: In bowl, whisk together flours with salt and pepper.
Add water, herbs and oil to flour mixture and beat with whisk until smooth. (May also be processed in blender.)
Let batter rest at least 30 minutes.

Prepare crêpe pan by oiling lightly. Pour 1/4 cup of batter into pan, tipping pan so batter thins to about 6-inch circle. Cook 30 seconds, until crêpe is golden brown on bottom. Flip, cook another 30 seconds.
If necessary, thin batter with more water to maintain consistency of light cream.

recipes.name: COCONUT-CASHEW FROSTING
instructions: In 2 1/2 quart pot, combine coconut milk and agar flakes. Let sit for 10 minutes. Add salt, vanilla, and maple syrup.
Over medium-high heat, bring coconut milk mixture to boil, stirring often, while scraping agar from sides and bottom of pot.
Reduce heat to very low and simmer, partially covered, stirring and scraping often, until agar is dissolved, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Pour coconut mixture into shallow pan and chill until set (about 15 minutes in freezer or 30-40 minutes in refrigerator).
In food processor, combine coconut milk-agar mixture with cashew butter and coconut extract. Process until very smooth.

recipes.name: CORN PASTA
instructions: Pulse flour and cornmeal in food processor to evenly distribute and aerate. Add eggs, process until dough forms rough ball, about 30 seconds. If dough resembles small pebbles, add water, 1/2 teaspoon at a time; if dough sticks to sides of bowl, add flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, and process until dough forms rough ball.
Turn dough onto work surface; knead until dough is smooth, 1 to 2 minutes. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside for at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours to relax.
Sift flour and cornmeal onto work surface (or bowl) in mound and make hollow in middle. Break eggs into hollow. With fork, start to mix in flour from edge.

Gradually incorporate most of flour until viscous paste begins to form. Put fork to one side and, using both hands, heap remaining flour from outside over paste in middle. Work flour into paste. If paste does not absorb all flour, and if ingredients cannot be easily worked, add a little water.

Work in water with both thumbs, then press dough into ball and work in rest of flour. Knead dough by pushing out dough with heels of hands, then form it into ball again. Repeat this kneading action until dough has firm but slightly elastic consistency and no longer changes shape when you remove your hands. Cover with plastic wrap and rest minimum of fifteen minutes.

recipes.name: COUS-COUS

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive or melted coconut oil

instructions: In small sauté pan, roast cous-cous in oil until there is a nutty aroma (2 to 3 minutes).
Pour water over cous-cous. Cover cous-cous with lid and steam for 5-10 minutes until all liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with fork and serve.

recipes.name: CURRY STOCK
instructions: In 1-gallon stockpot, heat oil OR ghee. Add vegetables, herbs, spices, and salt.
Sweat for 15-20 minutes. Add 4 quarts filtered water.
Bring to boil, covered, lower heat and simmer 30 minutes, uncovered. Strain stock through chinois.

recipes.name: Family Style Bean Curd
instructions: Cut tofu into 6 (1/2-inch) slices, then into triangles.
Heat wok and add coconut oil. Prepare plate with paper towel for draining. Deep fry tofu until golden brown.
Transfer fried tofu to paper towel to drain. Let oil cool completely before removing from wok.
Place deep fried tofu in small pot with water to cover. Add shoyu and ginger juice.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Heat wok and add sesame oil. Add scallions and ginger root. When their aroma is imparted, add carrots, mushrooms, water chestnuts, and fried tofu to wok.
Add hot stock, shoyu, mirin, and brown rice syrup and cook for an additional 3 minutes.
Dissolve kuzu in cold water and add to wok. Simmer 1 minute. Adjust ginger juice and shoyu or tamari if necessary.
Serve over rice or noodles. Garnish with scallions.

recipes.name: FISH FUMET

ingredients.name: brown rice or apple cider vinegar

instructions: In medium stockpot, heat oil. Add bones and mirepoix and sweat for 10 to 15 minutes.
Add 2 1/2 quarts water, bouquet garni, vinegar and wine, if using.
Bring to boil, lower heat, and simmer for 30-40 minutes.
Strain stock, pressing firmly to extract as much liquid as possible, though fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth-lined chinois.
Note: Bouquet garni is 1 bay leaf, 3 or 4 parsley stems, 1 sprig fresh thyme, 8 peppercorns.

recipes.name: Flaky Biscuits

ingredients.name: chilled unsalted butter or 7 tablespoons chilled coconut oil

instructions: Preheat oven to 375° F and line half-sheet tray with parchment paper.
Sift flours, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon (if using) in medium sized bowl. Whisk to combine.
Cut fat into flour mixture until fat is crumbly and coated in flour. Crumbles should be about size of small peas or smaller.
Pour in milk or almond milk and gently mix with rubber spatula just until combined, being careful to not over-mix.

Transfer dough to lightly floured table and gently roll out to shape of rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick. With long edge facing you, fold in both short ends to meet in middle. Fold dough forward in half and very gently roll together to 3/4 inch or no thinner than 1/2-inch square. This folding technique will provide flaky layers if not over-worked and too flat.
Cut biscuits with lightly floured cookie cutter or sharp knife and transfer to sheet tray. If desired, brush tops with melted butter.
Bake for about 6 minutes and rotate pan in oven to ensure even browning. Continue baking for about another 10 minutes or until golden brown on top and slightly firm to touch.
Transfer to rack and cool.
Note: Brushing with coconut oil in place of butter is not recommended.

recipes.name: Flounder en Papillote

ingredients.name: stemmed and chopped fresh dill and tarragon

instructions: Preheat convection oven to 425°F.
In large bowl mix carrot, leeks, zucchini, peppers, shallots, garlic, salt, pepper, and fresh herbs.
Fold each sheet of parchment paper in half. Starting at folded edge, cut into half of heart shape (when fold is open it should be full heart shape).

Place 1 filet on one half of each of 4 parchment “hearts.” Divide vegetable mixture into 4 even portions, placing one portion atop each fish filet. Add 1 tablespoon wine or stock and 1 tablespoon olive atop each vegetable stack.

Seal papillotes by folding over edges of packet and crimping edges tight. Place each papillote on sheet pan and bake in oven for 10 minutes (depending how cold ingredients are) or until parchment is puffed and turning golden brown on top.

recipes.name: Flounder Roulades
instructions: Preheat conventional oven to 375°F.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in 12-inch sauté pan. Add onions and sweat until tender. Add zucchini and cook for 1-2 more minutes.
Transfer onion/zucchini mixture to bowl and stir in breadcrumbs, capers, and tomatoes.
Place fish filets on cutting board presentation side down. Divide filling mixture into even portions among filets.
Roll filets and transfer to baking dish drizzled with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil (seam side down).
Sprinkle butter and wine in pan along with sprigs of thyme.
Bake for 20 minutes.

recipes.name: FOCACCIA

ingredients.name: unbleached white flour or 1/2 white and 1/2 whole wheat bread flour

instructions: For the sponge: In medium bowl, mix sponge ingredients (yeast, rice syrup or honey, lukewarm water, and hi gluten flour) with whisk. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 20-30 minutes in warm place.
For the crust: Add potato, water, oil and salt to bowl with sponge. Add flour in 1/2 cup increments.
Remove dough from bowl, form dough into ball and knead on a floured work surface. Dough should be soft and a little sticky. Knead 8-10 minutes.
